title: Network Engineer Deployment & Support
description:
Mission

Groq is building high-performance AI infrastructure designed to make inference fast, predictable, and scalable. Our Network Engineering & Datacenter teams design and operate the systems that provide the compute, storage, and networking capabilities behind Groq's rapidly growing AI infrastructure.

We are looking for a Network Engineer, Deployment & Support to deploy, validate, and support the datacenter network infrastructure behind Groq's global AI infrastructure. As a Network Engineer, Deployment & Support, you will take network designs from implementation planning through production deployment and operational handoff. You will work across front-end, back-end, management, OOB networks, ensuring that switches, optics, cabling, and supporting infrastructure are installed, configured, validated, documented, and ready for production.

This is a hands-on engineering role requiring strong datacenter networking fundamentals, physical-layer expertise, structured troubleshooting, and the ability to drive deployments across multiple teams and vendors.

Responsibilities & opportunities in this role:

  • Deploy and validate network infrastructure across new and existing Groq datacenters, including front-end, back-end, and management networks.
  • Configure and validate switches, network interfaces, optics, cabling, and supporting infrastructure against approved network designs and implementation standards.
  • Develop and maintain detailed cutsheets, port-maps, cabling plans, implementation procedures, validation plans, and as-built documentation.
  • Drive network deployment execution end-to-end, directing and coordinating on-site datacenter technicians through physical rack/stack, cabling, and installation while owning configuration, validation, troubleshooting, and production handoff.
  • Validate physical connectivity and optical performance, including fiber polarity, insertion loss, OTDR traces, transceiver health, and link-level troubleshooting, coordinating remediation with datacenter technicians and vendor teams as needed.
  • Troubleshoot network and hardware failures across switches, optics, cabling, servers, and supporting infrastructure, and perform root cause analysis for deployment and production issues.
  • Manage hardware readiness for deployments, including device staging, rack/stack coordination, inventory and asset record updates, RMA coordination, spares, and vendor shipments.
  • Coordinate on-site deployment audits and execute established QA/QC processes to ensure infrastructure meets Groq standards.
  • Partner closely with engineering, operations, project teams, and vendors to identify and resolve blockers throughout deployment.
  • Provide technical support to global datacenter teams during and after deployments, including maintenance activities, incidents, troubleshooting, remediation, and break-fix events.
  • Develop tools and scripts that improve network deployment, hardware validation, configuration, testing, and operational workflows.
  • Capture lessons learned from deployments and contribute to global implementation standards, deployment playbooks, and repeatable validation processes.
  • Train internal teams and provide technical guidance on network deployment standards, troubleshooting procedures, and operational practices.

Ideal candidates have/are:

  • 6+ years of experience in datacenter networking, network deployment, network operations, or infrastructure engineering.
  • Strong hands-on experience deploying and troubleshooting Ethernet networks in large-scale datacenter environments, including high-speed links such as 100G, 200G, 400G, or 800G.
  • Experience configuring and validating datacenter switches and modern network fabrics, with working knowledge of BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, and CLOS/leaf-spine architectures.
  • Strong understanding of fiber-optic infrastructure, transceivers, breakout cabling, fiber polarity, insertion loss, OTDR testing, cable management, and physical installation best practices.
  • Experience working with datacenter implementation artifacts such as cutsheets, port maps, cable schedules, rack elevations, implementation procedures, and as-built documentation.
  • Hands-on experience with hardware staging, rack/stack, cabling, RMA processes, and other physical deployment workflows.
  • Ability to troubleshoot systematically across physical, network, hardware, and software layers and drive issues through root cause and resolution.
  • Experience developing deployment automation or operational tooling using Python, Ansible, APIs, or similar technologies.
  • Experience executing deployments across network engineering, datacenter operations, structured cabling providers, hardware vendors, and other infrastructure partners.
  • Strong ownership, communication, and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deployments and drive work to completion under demanding timelines.
  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving environments where deployment plans and requirements can evolve quickly.
  • Ability to travel to global datacenter locations for deployments, maintenance activities, and other site-specific needs.
  • Ability to participate in an on-call rotation supporting a 24/7 production environment.

Why Join Us
  • Purposeful Hiring: You’re not here by accident, and neither is anyone else. Every teammate is handpicked with intention because who we build matters.
  • Builders Wanted: You’re not just riding the rocket ship, you’re building it. Your work directly shapes the trajectory of our company.
  • Mission-Driven Work: We’re here to make a real impact. Our mission fuels everything we do.
  • Tackling Hard Problems: If easy isn’t your thing, you’re in the right place. We solve some of the most complex and exciting challenges in our space.
  • Excellence Is The Standard: High performance isn’t just encouraged, it’s the baseline. And it’s contagious.

If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you!

Compensation
Groq is committed to providing competitive compensation through our Total Cash philosophy, which incorporates potential bonus value directly into base pay. The total cash salary range for this position, which is inclusive of the potential bonus value, is $245,800 - 365,200, with individual placement determined by your geographic location, experience, skills, and alignment with internal compensation standards. This range is specific to candidates located in the United States. Compensation for international candidates will vary based on local market dynamics. Beyond cash compensation, Groq also offers a Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Program and a robust suite of employee benefits.

title: Frozen Food Supervisor
description:
Why choose us?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career? Join us for an exciting opportunity at Albertsons Companies, where innovation and customer service go hand-in-hand!

At Albertsons Companies, we are looking for someone who’s not just seeking a job, but someone who wants to make an impact. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead, innovate, and contribute to the growth of a company that values great service and lasting customer relationships. This position offers the chance to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that’s constantly evolving.


Position Summary

The Frozen Supervisor is responsible for the daily operation, presentation, and profitability of the Frozen Department. This position leads department associates, maintains inventory levels, ensures product quality and food safety compliance, and delivers an outstanding shopping experience through excellent merchandising and customer service. The Frozen Supervisor works closely with store leadership to achieve sales, labor, and shrink goals while maintaining company standards.

Key Responsibilities Department Operations
  • Oversee daily Frozen Department operations to ensure efficiency and accuracy.
  • Maintain proper inventory levels through ordering, receiving, stocking, and rotation of merchandise.
  • Ensure all frozen products are stored and displayed according to company and food safety standards.
  • Monitor department conditions and take corrective action to maintain cleanliness and organization.
  • Execute company merchandising plans, promotional displays, and seasonal programs.
Customer Service
  • Provide exceptional customer service and create a welcoming shopping environment.
  • Assist customers with product inquiries, special orders, and resolving concerns.
  • Promote customer loyalty through positive interactions and product knowledge.
Merchandising & Inventory Control
  • Maintain attractive, well-stocked, and properly signed displays.
  • Ensure accurate pricing and promotional execution.
  • Monitor product movement and adjust orders to maximize sales while minimizing shrink.
  • Perform inventory counts and assist with department financial controls.
Leadership & Team Development
  • Supervise, train, coach, and develop department associates.
  • Assign duties and monitor performance to ensure expectations are met.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, and a positive working environment.
  • Support hiring, onboarding, and performance management activities as directed by store leadership.
Food Safety & Compliance
  • Follow all food safety, sanitation, and workplace safety requirements.
  • Maintain proper product temperatures and equipment standards.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and operational procedures.
Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Previous grocery retail or frozen department experience preferred.
  • Prior supervisory or leadership experience preferred.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Basic math and computer skills.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to frequently lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and perform repetitive motions for extended periods.
  • Ability to work in refrigerated and freezer environments.
  • Flexible availability, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
Key Success Factors
  • Strong leadership and team-building abilities.
  • Effective inventory and shrink management.
  • Commitment to customer service excellence.
  • Attention to detail and execution of department standards.
  • Ability to drive sales while maintaining operational efficiency.

We also provide a variety of benefits including:

  • Competitive wages paid weekly
· Access to up to 50% of your earned wages before payday, via our partnership with Stream
  • Associate discounts
  • Health and financial well-being benefits for eligible associates (Medical, Dental, 401k and more!)
  • Time off (vacation, holidays, sick pay). For eligibility requirements please visit myACI Benefits

  • An inclusive work environment with talented colleagues who reflect the communities we serve

title: Software Development Engineer
description:
Job Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, and maintain networking software for current and future network and security products.
  • Implement and enhance network protocols and features, including routing, switching, network services, and secure connectivity.
  • Investigate and resolve network connectivity, interoperability, performance, and stability issues.
  • Analyze packet flows and optimize network processing for reliability and efficiency.
  • Collaborate with hardware, firmware, and QA teams to integrate features and validate functionality across different network environments.
  • Participate in software design, code reviews, testing, and technical documentation.
  • Support troubleshooting and resolution of customer-reported network issues.
  • Deliver high-quality software on schedule and communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.

Job Requirements:

  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in networking-related software development.
  • Strong C/C++ programming experience in a Unix/Linux environment is essential.
  • Solid understanding of TCP/IP networking, Ethernet, IPv4/IPv6, switching, and routing.
  • Hands-on experience implementing or maintaining network protocols and features, such as VLAN, DHCP, DNS, NAT, multicast, routing protocols, or VPN.
  • Strong understanding of packet forwarding, routing tables, network interfaces, and protocol state machines.
  • Experience with Linux network programming, including sockets, inter-process communication, and event-driven or multithreaded applications.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills using packet captures, protocol analysis, system logs, and debugging tools such as Wireshark, tcpdump, and GDB.
  • Familiarity with network configuration and testing in environments involving routers, switches, firewalls, and end devices.
  • Knowledge of secure coding practices, software testing, and network protocol interoperability testing.
  • Experience with Git, code reviews, and maintaining production software.
  • Knowledge of network security technologies, including IPsec, TLS, authentication, and access control, is a plus.
  • Experience with Linux kernel networking, network drivers, hardware acceleration, or embedded networking platforms is a plus.
  • Knowledge of Shell or Python scripting for network testing and automation is a plus.

Educational Requirements:

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience; M.S. preferred.

description:
Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data.

The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity.

Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control.

For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production.

Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide.

  • Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments.
  • Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies.
  • Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures.
  • We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team connects market insight, data quality, and operational execution to help Immuta make better business decisions. We work across the organization to improve how the company understands its market, prioritizes opportunities, measures performance, and turns data into action.

This role sits at the intersection of data science, analytics engineering, and business strategy. Reporting to the Director of Growth Operations, you’ll join a lean, hands-on team where success depends on combining strong technical judgment with practical business understanding. Your work will help establish trusted data workflows, evaluate the signals that matter, and improve how Immuta makes decisions about accounts, opportunities, and revenue programs.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Data Scientist, you’ll own the path from raw data to decisions that leaders can act on. You’ll bring new data into Snowflake, model it in dbt to production standards, investigate open questions about Immuta’s market and revenue motion, and build the evidence behind better decisions.

You’ll work on questions such as which intent and engagement signals meaningfully precede opportunity creation, whether account-readiness scores predict conversion, how partner overlap relates to deal outcomes, and how to evaluate event performance while accounting for pre-existing buyer intent.

This is a highly hands-on, individual contributor role for someone who enjoys working across the full data lifecycle. You’ll be expected to define the question, choose an appropriate analytical approach, communicate uncertainty clearly, and help stakeholders move from analysis to action.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the reliability of the revenue pipeline data used for business reporting and decision-making. Investigate data issues, identify root causes, resolve problems, and document definitions and validation practices.
  • Bring new data sources into Snowflake, including enrichment, intent, partner, and product-usage data, using Snowpipe, APIs, and related tools, and build and maintain production-quality dbt models that make data reliable, reusable, and accessible to business and technical stakeholders.
  • Translate ambiguous business questions into testable hypotheses with clearly defined outcomes and success criteria.
  • Build, validate, and improve scoring and prioritization models, including account-readiness, ideal customer profile, and lead-qualification models.
  • Apply regression, hypothesis testing, experimental and quasi-experimental design, and uncertainty quantification to questions involving small, incomplete, or messy business datasets.
  • Communicate findings, recommendations, assumptions, and limitations to business leaders and other stakeholders in a way that supports clear decision-making.
  • Automate recurring analysis and reporting so that repeatable questions can be answered through reliable workflows rather than manual effort.
  • Improve documentation, analytical standards, and data practices as the Growth and Revenue Operations function scales.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • Experience: 5+ years of experience in data science, quantitative analytics, analytics engineering, or a related field.
  • Preferred Experience: Familiarity with a business intelligence tool such as Looker or Tableau, and/or experience working with go-to-market or revenue data.
  • Statistical Methods: Strong applied-statistics foundation, including regression, hypothesis testing, experimental design, quasi-experimental methods, and reasoning with small or imperfect samples.
  • Python: Proficiency using Python for analysis and modeling, including tools such as pandas, statsmodels, scikit-learn, or comparable libraries.
  • SQL: Advanced SQL skills, including the ability to work with complex data models, validate results, and investigate data-quality issues.
  • Data Platforms: Production experience with dbt or a comparable data-transformation framework, along with experience bringing data into a warehouse through APIs, Snowpipe, or comparable ingestion tools.
  • Business Impact: A track record of translating analysis into recommendations that influenced a business decision, operating practice, or strategic priority, along with the ability to explain technical analysis and business implications to leadership and non-technical stakeholders.
BENEFITS
At Immuta, our goal is to help bridge the gap between personal and professional growth, so that our team members can be well and thrive personally and professionally. After all, great professional success stories rarely happen without great personal success stories! Our generous benefits package given to all full time employees includes:
  • 100% employer paid Healthcare (Medical, Dental, Vision) premiums for you and your dependents (including Domestic Partners)
  • Stock Options
  • Paid parental leave (Both Maternity and Paternity)
  • Unlimited Paid time off (U.S. based positions)
  • Learning and Development Resources
EEO NOTICE: Immuta provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, age, disability (including disability due to pregnancy) or genetics, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Immuta complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment.
NOTICE TO THIRD PARTY RECRUITERS: Immuta does not accept candidates from third party recruiters. All candidates submitted through are considered to be submissions by the candidate and no submission will obligate Immuta to pay any third party for the referral or hiring of a candidate.

title: Skilled Trades Program Manager
description:
Position Summary:

The Skilled Trades Program Manager is responsible for coordinating the development, implementation, and daily operations of Salem University's skilled trades certificate and diploma programs. This position supports the University's commitment to providing accessible, career-focused education that prepares students for employment, industry-recognized credentials, and continued educational opportunities.

The Program Manager provides operational coordination across program scheduling, instructional resources, instructor engagement, student success initiatives, workforce partnerships, and continuous improvement activities. The position works collaboratively with the Office of the Provost, designated academic leadership, faculty, Admissions, Academic Advising, the Registrar, Institutional Effectiveness, Information Technology, Marketing, and other University departments to support effective program delivery.

The position also supports the development and implementation of innovative instructional approaches, including hands-on training, competency-based learning, simulation, augmented reality, virtual reality, and other appropriate educational technologies.

The Skilled Trades Program Manager serves in an operational and program coordination capacity. Final academic oversight and authority remain with the Office of the Provost and designated academic leadership, including responsibility for academic standards, curriculum approval, faculty qualifications, accreditation requirements, and academic policy decisions.

Success in this position requires strong organizational skills, technical or workforce education experience, effective collaboration, operational accountability, and a commitment to student achievement and workforce readiness.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The duties listed below are representative of the responsibilities of this position. Additional duties may be assigned based on departmental or institutional needs.

Program Coordination & Operations

  • Coordinate daily operations of Salem University's skilled trades certificate and diploma programs.
  • Support the development, implementation, and launch of approved workforce-focused certificate and diploma offerings.
  • Coordinate course schedules, instructional resources, faculty assignments, training activities, and program delivery across approved instructional modalities.
  • Collaborate with academic leadership to support curriculum consistency, instructional quality, and alignment with established program outcomes.
  • Maintain organized program schedules, instructional documentation, operational procedures, and related records.
  • Monitor enrollment, student progression, course completion, credential attainment, and other established program performance indicators.
  • Identify operational challenges and recommend improvements to strengthen program efficiency, effectiveness, and student success.
  • Coordinate program resources and operational requirements to support timely and consistent instructional delivery.
  • Communicate program needs, operational concerns, and recommendations to designated academic leadership.
  • Support implementation of approved program changes and institutional initiatives.


Curriculum Development & Instructional Innovation

  • Collaborate with faculty, academic leadership, and industry partners to support the development and continuous improvement of workforce-aligned curricula.
  • Assist in identifying technical competencies, practical skills, occupational standards, and industry expectations relevant to skilled trades education.
  • Support the integration of appropriate instructional technologies, including simulation, augmented reality, virtual reality, artificial intelligence, and digital learning platforms.
  • Coordinate opportunities to incorporate industry-recognized certifications, micro-credentials, and competency-based learning experiences into approved academic programs.
  • Support the development of hands-on instructional activities, practical assessments, technical demonstrations, and industry-relevant learning experiences.
  • Research workforce trends, emerging technologies, and evolving industry standards to identify opportunities for program enhancement.
  • Provide recommendations regarding instructional resources, equipment, technologies, and training methodologies.
  • Collaborate with academic leadership to evaluate proposed program improvements and new credential opportunities.
  • Ensure proposed curriculum changes and instructional innovations are submitted through established University academic review and approval processes.
  • Support implementation of approved curriculum and instructional improvements.


Faculty & Instructor Coordination

  • Assist with identifying and recruiting qualified industry instructors, faculty, and technical training professionals.
  • Coordinate instructor onboarding, scheduling, instructional resources, and program-related communication.
  • Provide operational support to instructors regarding course schedules, training resources, program procedures, and established University expectations.
  • Collaborate with designated academic leadership to support instructional quality and consistent program delivery.
  • Provide operational feedback regarding instructor needs, scheduling concerns, training requirements, and professional-development opportunities.
  • Support instructors and on-site proctors in coordinating student learning activities and required technical competencies.
  • Promote effective communication among instructors, academic leadership, and student support departments.
  • Coordinate instructional resources and equipment necessary for effective program delivery.
  • Refer faculty performance, academic evaluation, instructional compliance, and related academic matters to designated academic leadership.
  • Support the implementation of approved instructional standards and faculty development initiatives.


Student Success & Academic Support

  • Collaborate with Academic Advising, Student Success, faculty, and program leadership to support student retention, persistence, and credential completion.
  • Monitor student progression, attendance, academic engagement, and completion outcomes to identify potential barriers to student success.
  • Coordinate appropriate interventions and referrals for students experiencing academic or operational challenges.
  • Assist students in understanding program expectations, technical competency requirements, course sequencing, and available University resources.
  • Support career readiness activities, including preparation for industry-recognized certifications and employment opportunities.
  • Collaborate with the Registrar and designated academic leadership regarding academic planning, credit evaluations, and individualized learning plans when applicable.
  • Support timely resolution of student concerns through established University communication and academic leadership channels.
  • Coordinate communication regarding program schedules, instructional requirements, and student participation expectations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve student engagement, persistence, and program completion.
  • Maintain appropriate confidentiality of student information and comply with applicable University policies and FERPA requirements.


Workforce Development & Industry Partnerships

  • Develop and maintain professional relationships with employers, workforce development organizations, trade associations, and industry professionals.
  • Support partnerships that enhance student training, employment pathways, industry certifications, and workforce development opportunities.
  • Collaborate with industry partners to identify emerging workforce needs and recommend relevant certificate and diploma offerings.
  • Support opportunities for apprenticeships, internships, employer-sponsored training, and work-based learning experiences when appropriate.
  • Assist with identifying potential grant opportunities, industry sponsorships, equipment partnerships, and workforce development resources.
  • Collaborate with Admissions and Marketing to support accurate program representation, student recruitment, and awareness of career opportunities.
  • Promote Salem University's skilled trades programs through professional relationships, industry engagement, and community partnerships.
  • Gather employer feedback regarding workforce competencies, technical skills, and training expectations.
  • Communicate industry trends and potential program opportunities to academic leadership.
  • Coordinate approved partnership activities in collaboration with appropriate University departments.


Program Assessment, Accreditation & Regulatory Support

  • Support institutional assessment, program review, and continuous improvement processes for skilled trades certificate and diploma programs.
  • Coordinate the collection and organization of data related to student learning outcomes, enrollment, retention, completion, credential attainment, and workforce outcomes.
  • Collaborate with Institutional Effectiveness and academic leadership to support accurate program reporting and assessment activities.
  • Assist designated academic leadership and Regulatory Affairs with documentation required for institutional accreditation, state authorization, and applicable regulatory reporting.
  • Maintain organized documentation supporting program effectiveness, instructional quality, and continuous improvement.
  • Support compliance with approved University policies, instructional standards, and program requirements.
  • Collaborate with academic leadership to ensure program descriptions, instructional activities, and industry credential representations accurately reflect approved program expectations.
  • Identify potential compliance concerns and communicate them promptly to the Office of the Provost and appropriate University personnel.
  • Support implementation of approved corrective actions and program improvement initiatives.
  • Participate in program review, assessment, and compliance activities as assigned.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication

  • Collaborate with Academic Affairs, Admissions, Academic Advising, Student Success, Registrar, Institutional Effectiveness, Information Technology, Marketing, and other University departments.
  • Coordinate operational requirements necessary to support program development and delivery.
  • Communicate program updates, scheduling changes, resource needs, and operational concerns to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Participate in program planning meetings and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Provide timely updates regarding program performance, implementation progress, and operational challenges.
  • Support effective communication among faculty, instructors, students, academic leadership, and administrative departments.
  • Identify opportunities to improve coordination and operational processes across departments.
  • Escalate matters requiring academic, regulatory, financial, or institutional approval through established University channels.


Program Performance & Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor established program performance indicators and operational objectives.
  • Review enrollment trends, course completion, student persistence, credential attainment, and other available program outcomes.
  • Identify operational barriers affecting program delivery and student success.
  • Recommend process improvements to strengthen program effectiveness and efficiency.
  • Support the implementation of approved improvements and monitor progress toward established objectives.
  • Maintain accurate records and provide periodic operational reports to designated leadership.
  • Utilize available data and stakeholder feedback to support informed recommendations.
  • Contribute to the University's workforce education initiatives and institutional growth objectives.


Professional & University Responsibilities

  • Represent Salem University's mission, values, and institutional priorities professionally.
  • Maintain appropriate professional relationships with students, faculty, staff, employers, and community partners.
  • Exercise sound judgment and accountability in coordinating assigned program responsibilities.
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, employee, institutional, and partnership information.
  • Follow applicable University policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Participate in required meetings, professional-development activities, and institutional initiatives.
  • Maintain awareness of developments in skilled trades education, workforce development, and instructional technology.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.


Academic Oversight & Institutional Accountability

The Skilled Trades Program Manager serves in a program coordination and operational management capacity under the direction of the Office of the Provost and designated academic leadership.

While the position supports curriculum development, instructor coordination, program assessment, and regulatory documentation, final academic authority remains with the Office of the Provost and designated academic leadership.

The Program Manager does not independently:

  • Approve academic curricula or modifications to established academic programs.
  • Establish or modify faculty qualification standards.
  • Make final academic policy determinations.
  • Approve academic assessments or grading decisions reserved for faculty or academic leadership.
  • Authorize changes requiring institutional, accreditation, or regulatory approval.
  • Commit the University to new academic programs, credentials, or instructional requirements without appropriate authorization.

All program development, curriculum modifications, instructional requirements, and academic decisions must follow Salem University's established governance and approval processes.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Associate degree in a relevant field or an institutionally approved equivalent combination of technical training, recognized industry credentials, and progressively responsible professional experience.
  • Approximately three to five years of related experience in skilled trades, technical education, workforce development, industrial operations, construction, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating programs, projects, training activities, or operational processes.
  • Working knowledge of skilled trades practices, industry competencies, workforce development trends, and career-focused education.
  • Strong organizational, interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with instructors, academic leadership, employers, and cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, coordinate resources, and meet established deadlines.
  • Demonstrated commitment to student success, workforce readiness, professional accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to work within established academic policies, accreditation requirements, and institutional procedures.
  • Demonstrated commitment to maintaining accurate program documentation and supporting data-informed decision-making.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in construction management, Construction Technology, Business, Workforce Development, Education, or a closely related field.
  • Recognized trade certification, technical credential, or journeyperson license in a relevant skilled trades discipline.
  • Experience teaching, training, or supporting adult learners in higher education, technical education, apprenticeship, or workforce development environments.
  • Experience coordinating certificate, diploma, technical training, or industry credential programs.
  • Previous experience working with community colleges, universities, technical schools, workforce organizations, or employer-sponsored training programs.
  • Experience developing or supporting workforce-aligned curricula, competency-based learning, and industry-recognized certifications.
  • Familiarity with instructional technologies, including simulation, augmented reality, virtual reality, digital learning platforms, or artificial intelligence.
  • Experience developing employer partnerships, apprenticeship opportunities, or industry training collaborations.
  • Understanding of institutional accreditation, academic assessment, and higher education regulatory requirements.


Physical Requirements

The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position.

  • Ability to perform work involving regular computer use, written communication, and electronic record management.
  • Ability to attend meetings, instructional activities, program events, and industry engagement opportunities.
  • Ability to move between classrooms, laboratories, training spaces, and other assigned University facilities as needed.
  • Ability to observe instructional activities and technical training environments.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with students, instructors, faculty, employers, and University personnel.
  • Ability to perform duties in office, classroom, laboratory, and other approved training environments.
  • Ability to travel to employer or workforce development meetings when required by assigned responsibilities.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.


Work Environment

The position operates within an academic and workforce education environment and may involve work in administrative offices, classrooms, technical training laboratories, instructional facilities, and employer or community partner locations.

The position may require coordination across multiple University departments and instructional environments.

Depending on assigned programs, the employee may encounter equipment, tools, machinery, and other materials associated with skilled trades instruction. Applicable safety procedures and required protective equipment must be followed when entering or working within designated training areas.

Work schedules and travel expectations will be determined by operational requirements and the approved position arrangement.


Equal Employment Opportunity

Salem University is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.


Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.


Job Description Disclaimer

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by individuals assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications. Salem University reserves the right to modify responsibilities as institutional needs evolve.

description:
Billing Specialist

General Information

Job Title: Billing Specialist

Department: Billing

Reports to: Revenue Cycle Manager/Revenue Cycle Team Lead

Location: Arlington, TX

Employee Type: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Non-exempt - Hourly


Job Summary

The billing specialist is responsible for coordinating patient and insurance billing for our multi-specialty orthopedic group and providing patient care excellence by performing the following duties:

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

  • Responsible for following entire revenue cycle from charge entry through insurance and patient payments.
  • Work through an electronic claims worklist to follow up with insurance companies to investigate status of claims. Appeal denials, resubmit claims, send medical records and process any additional information as needed.
  • Work in partnership with Athena to ensure claims have processed correctly and payments have been posted correctly.
  • Answers telephone, and responds to inquiries from insurance carriers, patients, and co-workers.
  • Investigate and resolve billing discrepancies resulting in overpaid/underpaid accounts.
  • Establishes payment plans to help patients manage payment of bills.
  • Confers with doctors, nurses, and other health personnel to assure complete, current, and accurate medical records.
  • Operates computer to process, store, and retrieve health information.
  • Communicate any trends, discrepancies, and underpayments to the Revenue Cycle Manager immediately.
  • Submit refunds for processing by the Revenue Cycle Manager.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Job Qualifications

Education

High school diploma or general education degree (GED). Two to three years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience a must.

Specific Job Experience

  • Ability to maintain the confidentiality and security of sensitive, privileged communications and work product.
  • Ability to utilize Electronic Heath Care Record system for documentation to patients’ account/record.
  • Knowledge of third-party insurance and billing practices
  • Knowledge of ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS codes and documentation guidelines required.

  • Previous medical billing and surgery billing experience required.
  • Experience with billing program software, Athena, preferred.
  • Working knowledge of commercial and government insurance
  • Coding/Billing Certification Preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong computer skills
  • Effective communication skills
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Prior customer service representative experience required.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Applications. (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)

title: Department Manager Meat-Valdez
description:
Job Description

Job Title: Meat Manager

Reports to: Store Director

Salaried or Hourly: Hourly

Job Code: 000740, 100584

Department: Meat

Date: March 2015

Position Purpose: To direct the operation of the Meat Department, including supervising and training personnel. Ensures customer service and product quality, freshness, safety and selection.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities:

  • Champions Company and Division customer service programs to meet or exceed Division customer service goals. Handles customer relations in a positive manner, including effective resolution of customer complaints. Promotes Albertson’s philosophy of personalized service.

  • Supervising the day to day functions of the meat department to achieve customer service, and sales and profit objectives.

  • Supervises, motivates, directs, trains and participates in the hiring of meat department personnel. Monitors associate performance and recommend personnel actions such as hiring, firing, layoff and disciplinary actions. Schedules personnel to ensure adequate coverage and service levels and to meet department budgetary objectives.

  • Conducts daily inspections of all meat sections and initiates corrective measures to ensure compliance with product quality and trimming and grinding procedures, rotates products, maintains in stock conditions, code date standards, and sanitation, safety and security requirements.

  • Assists with all meat department duties such as: receiving, storage, cleaning, customer service, cutting, grinding, wrapping and packaging and stocking.

  • Implements effective promotional and seasonal displays. Controls shrink and expenses. Accurately completes and monitors daily log sheet, purchase report, and sales and labor and other required paperwork and logs. Maintains records on ad items movement.

  • Orders, checks, receives and controls inventory to ensure adequate and proper inventory level, product quality and freshness and to prevent the sale of out of code products. Takes periodic inventories, processes administrative paperwork and maintains accurate department records. Maintains and organizes meat department cooler and freezer.

  • Ensures that product quality, trimming, grinding, packaging, labeling, rotation and wrapping standards are met.

  • Ensures proper merchandising of product by understanding and implementing schematics, merchandising of advertised items, proper signing procedures and monitoring product flow. Complies with retail labeling laws, federal and state regulations and Company policies.

  • Follows Company policy in pricing and handling re-worked and reduced-to-clear items. Complies with all federal, state and local health, and food handling and safety standards.

  • Checks competitors for comparisons on prices, product variety and merchandising procedures.

  • Handles customer relation. Assists customers by taking and filling special orders. Makes product suggestions and engages in suggestive selling. May make intercom announcements.

  • Ensures cleanliness and sanitation of sales floor and work area, freezer and cooler, equipment, and retail cases.

  • Answering and responding incoming calls appropriately. Receives and appropriately resolves customer complaints and reports to the Store Director as appropriate.

  • Attends required training.

  • Maintains and cleans knives, scales, steamers, display cases, saws, meat tenderizers, slicers, cubers and wrapping equipment.

  • Assists with implementing emergency procedures in the event of equipment and computer software malfunctions.

  • Ensures that all associates are trained and instructed in the proper performance of work duties. Monitors associate performance and reports observations to the Store Director. Resolves associate complaints and reports to the Store Director as appropriate.

  • Maintains confidentiality concerning associates, store sales and other Company information.

  • Responsible for performing all job duties and responsibilities safely, accurately and with honesty and integrity.

  • Other necessary and required duties.

Skills and Physical Requirements:

  • Requires working knowledge of all job duties within the Meat Department including cutting, wrapping, steaming, grinding, cubing, tenderizing and customer service.

  • Requires strong communication skills, good leadership and interpersonal skills, the proven ability to manage people and the ability to maintain composure in dealing with customers and co-workers.

  • Requires knowledge of employment laws and workplace practices.

  • Requires a good understanding of company policies and Meat Department policies and procedures. Requires the ability to judge and react to business activity.

  • Must have knowledge of product variety, standards, perishability, food safety, sanitation, labeling and department policies and procedures.

  • Frequently reaches, lifts, stacks and maneuvers objects of varying dimensions and weights up to approx­imately 80 lbs. Bends, stoops and reaches frequently and occasionally climbs ladders. Pushes and pulls fully loaded hand trucks, high boys and pallet jacks. Performs repetitious arm movement to prepare and package products.

  • Manual dexterity and good eye-hand coordination are necessary. Must be able to operate meat cutting utensils and equipment.

  • Mental alertness is necessary to ensure safe and accurate completion of work activities. Requires knowledge of basic mathematics and weights and measures. Must have knowledge of taste, content and perishability of products, safety and sanitation procedures and department policies and procedures.

  • Operates computer software and electronic ordering devices to order products, plan sales, input inventory and schedules, and print labels.

  • Utilizes knives, saws, cutters, grinders and other cutting equipment. Utilizes cleaning supplies and equipment. Utilizes safety cutters. Requires use of safety gloves.

  • Knowledge of profit and loss statements.

  • Will be required to work nights, weekends and holidays. Scheduled hours will vary. Good attendance is required.

  • Exposure to potential hazards exists with respect to cutting equipment and other work aids necessary to perform job duties.

    Work Environment:

  • Hands remain moist during majority of work time. Requires the ability to work for prolonged periods of time in an environment with a temperature range of 40˚ to 50˚ Fahrenheit.

  • Exposure to 35˚ Fahrenheit while handling products in cold cases, 28˚ Fahrenheit in cooler and -20 degrees Fahrenheit in freezer.

  • Working conditions consist of a temperature controlled store environment.

Safety – Sensitive Position:

Job responsibilities include tasks or duties that could affect the safety or health of the employee performing the task or others.

DISCLAIMER:

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of work performed by employees assigned to this job. If you have questions regarding your ability to physically perform the listed job duties and requirements – e.g. lifting, standing, bending, etc. - please speak to your Store Director. All team members must comply with Company, Division, and Store policies and applicable laws. The responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified may vary within each store and from store to store.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Description

:

About the role

St Vincent’s Health Australia has committed, through Strategy 2030, to connecting care across its public hospitals, private hospitals, aged care and virtual care services, with half of all care delivered virtually or in people’s homes by 2030.


As a Data Engineer, you will manage and develop the data pipelines that feed St Vincent’s Health Australia’s enterprise data platform and underpin reporting, analytics, machine learning and emerging Generative AI solutions.

You will:

  • Build and maintain trusted data pipelines that support reporting, analytics, machine learning and AI use cases across the organisation.
  • Work with modern Microsoft data technologies, including Azure Data Factory, Azure SQL, Power BI, Databricks or Microsoft Fabric.
  • Shape data models, integration patterns and engineering standards for the enterprise data platform.
  • Work closely with business, technical and governance stakeholders to ensure data is secure, governed, accurate and fit for purpose.

Key responsibilities of the role

  • Design, build, and maintain end-to-end ETL/ELT pipelines to profile, cleanse, and integrate multi-source data across modern platforms like Azure Data Factory, Azure SQL, Databricks or Microsoft Fabric.
  • Design enterprise data architectures and dimensional models (facts, dimensions, hierarchies) while evaluating risks and impacts.
  • Monitor and maintain data warehouse environments to ensure high reliability, optimal performance, and cost efficiency.
  • Apply software engineering best practices to data solutions, including Git version control, CI/CD automation, testing, and configuration management.
  • Implement robust security, access controls, data lineage, and automated quality checks within established governance frameworks.
  • Build, enhance, and integrate master-data capabilities across enterprise reporting and analytics platforms.
  • Create and maintain tabular data models using Power BI, Azure Analysis Services, and SSAS.
  • Provide operational troubleshooting for production services and participate in scheduled after-hours support when required.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, system configuration records, support guides, and training materials.
  • Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to communicate system updates, resolve issues, and ensure data products meet business requirements.

Things that work for us

  • Minimum five years of experience across data engineering, modeling, architecture, and warehousing, supported by a tertiary qualification in Information Technology, Health Informatics, or a related discipline.
  • Proven experience designing and building enterprise ETL/ELT solutions using Microsoft Azure, Azure Data Factory, and modern lakehouse architectures such as Databricks or Microsoft Fabric.
  • Advanced SQL capabilities alongside strong programming proficiency in Python or Scala for data manipulation, pipeline engineering, and automation.
  • Deep understanding of data warehouse architecture and dimensional modeling methodologies, combined with strong data profiling, cleansing, and systems analysis skills.
  • Demonstrated experience developing analytical reporting solutions, including secure Power BI dashboards and tabular models across Azure Analysis Services and SSAS.
  • Strong implementation of software engineering best practices (Git, CI/CD, automated testing), with desirable exposure to Infrastructure as Code and containerization.
  • High-regard experience or practical exposure to modern AI concepts, including Generative AI (Azure OpenAI, RAG, prompt engineering), vector databases, and predictive analytics.
  • Excellent communication, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement skills, with an understanding of healthcare data privacy standards and the flexibility to support operational requirements and occasional on-site travel.

Things that work for you

  • Permanent, full-time role based in Melbourne with hybrid working (minimum two day a week on site)
  • Competitive salary packaging options
  • Discounted private health insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program for staff and their families
  • Access to the Fitness Passport (FP)

Why become part of St Vincent’s Health Australia

Because you’re like us, you believe in our vision that every person, whoever and wherever they are, is served with excellent and compassionate care, by a better and fairer health and aged care system. Better for all our people, who work tirelessly to provide the highest levels of care and quality of life for our patients and clients. And better support for the local communities we play an important role in and continue to support.

title: Medarbejdere til sagsbehandling i internationale sager om familieydelse
description:
I Internationale familieydelser i ATP koordinerer vi børne- og ungeydelser på tværs af Europa for vandrende arbejdstagere. Du er derfor med til at sikre, at børnefamilier får de ydelser, de har krav på – også når livet, familien og arbejdet foregår på tværs af lande.

Dine opgaver bliver at:

  • skriftligt koordinere ydelser på tværs af Europa gennem vores fagsystem
  • indhente oplysninger, partshøre og træffe afgørelser med borger i fokus.
  • rådgive borgere og udenlandske myndigheder telefonisk
  • bidrage til forbedringer i arbejdsgange og service
  • samarbejde tæt med kolleger i en specialiseret afdeling.

Det får du hos os

  • Et meningsfuldt job, hvor din indsats direkte betyder noget for borgere.
  • Faglige udfordringer, for du lærer hurtigt at navigere i EU-regler og dansk lovgivning.
  • Variation i hverdagen, da du både arbejder med skriftlig sagsbehandling og telefonisk vejledning (primært skriftligt).
  • Mulighed for at byde ind på udviklingsopgaver som procesoptimering, kunderejser eller generelle dataforbedringer.
  • Et godt team, hvor vi sparrer, hjælper hinanden og prioriterer et godt arbejdsmiljø.
  • Fleksibilitet og balance, fordi vi sætter barren højt, men også ved, at energi uden for jobbet er vigtigt.

Hvem er du?

Du kan være nyuddannet eller have erfaring, men det vigtigste er, at du:

  • arbejder struktureret og kan bevare overblikket i komplekse sager
  • er skarp til skriftlig formidling på dansk
  • kan kommunikere på engelsk (andre sprog er et plus)
  • tager ansvar, men også er en holdspiller
  • er nysgerrig, stiller spørgsmål og lærer hurtigt nyt

Har du allerede erfaring med sagsbehandling i et lovreguleret område, er det en klar fordel.

Sådan ansøger du

Send os dit CV senest søndag den 22. november. Når du sender dit CV via vores system, får du mulighed for kort at beskrive din motivation for at søge stillingen.

I ATP arbejder vi for en fair rekrutteringsproces, og derfor beder vi dig om ikke at vedhæfte billede i dit CV eller angive din alder, når du søger.

Vi ansætter på baggrund af kompetencer og potentiale og opfordrer alle til at søge stillingen – uanset køn og kønsidentitet, etnicitet, national, social og kulturel baggrund, religion eller tro, seksuel orientering, funktionsnedsættelse og alder.

Du kan læse mere om rekrutteringsforløbet her:

Vi behandler ansøgninger løbende og forventer tiltrædelse senest 1. februar 2027.

Har du spørgsmål, kan du kontakte sektionschef Nina Nors Skallebæk Nielsen på tlf. 51 72 44 83 eller mail: nnn@atp.dk

Af sikkerhedsmæssige årsager og for at beskytte værdier og datainfrastruktur beder vi om straffeattest, kopi af dit pas og eventuelt eksamensbevis. Straffeattesten må ikke give anledning til bemærkninger, og dokumenterne slettes umiddelbart efter vurdering.

Til annoncører og rekrutteringsbureauer: ATP frabeder sig uopfordrede henvendelser om annoncering, kandidater, produkter og ydelser i forbindelse med stillingsopslag og rekrutteringer. Vi beder om, at dette respekteres, og at vores ledere og medarbejdere ikke kontaktes i den henseende.

description:
Working Arrangements & Further Information

The MoJ offers Hybrid Working arrangements where business need allows. This is an informal, non-contractual form of flexible working that blends working from your base location, different MoJ sites and / or from home (please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas). All employees will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of their working time in an office, subject to local estate capacity.

Some roles will not be suitable for Hybrid Working. Similarly, Hybrid Working will not suit everyone’s circumstances. Arrangements will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate(s) and subject to regular review.

For nationally advertised role: all successful candidates will be appointed to the nearest viable office nearest to their home postcode and on its respective pay scale. This will be at either a HQ building (subject to desk allocation, a Justice Collaboration Centre (JCC) or a Justice Satellite Office (JSO) – See Map. All employees will be expected to spend a minimum of 60% of their working time in an office, subject to local estate capacity).

For current MoJ employees, your base location will need to be changed to the nearest viable office (to your home postcode), either at a HQ building, JCC or JSO within the National Office Network and moved its location’s respective pay scale (any legacy arrangements/locations will need to be amended).

Some of MoJ’s terms and conditions of service are changing as part of Civil Service reform. The changes will apply to staff joining MoJ who are new to the Civil Service. Staff joining MoJ from other civil service employers will transfer onto the new MoJ terms if they are already on 'modernised' terms in their current post or onto 'unmodernised' MoJ terms if they are on 'unmodernised' terms at their current post. Details will be available if an offer is made.

MoJ candidates who are on a specialist grade, will be able to retain their grade on lateral transfer.

All candidates who are currently in receipt of Mark Time / Pay Protection should ensure they are familiar with the new policy on permanent and temporary promotion which can be found on the employee intranet.

Flexible working hours

The Ministry of Justice offers a flexible working system in many offices. Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week. MoJ welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the MoJ’s Flexible Working policy.

Benefits

The MoJ offers a range of benefits:

Annual Leave

Annual leave is 25 days on appointment and will increase to 30 days after five years’ service.

There is also a scheme to allow qualifying staff to buy or sell up to three days leave each year. Additional paid time off for public holidays and 1 privilege day. Leave for part-time and job share posts will be calculated on a pro-rata basis.

Pension

The Civil Service offers a choice of pension schemes, giving you the flexibility to choose the pension that suits you best.

Training

The Ministry of Justice is committed to staff development and offers an extensive range of training and development opportunities.

Networks

The opportunity to join employee-run networks that have been established to provide advice and support and to enable the views of employees from minority groups to be expressed direct to senior management. There are currently networks for employees of minority ethnic origin, employees with disabilities, employees with caring responsibilities, women employees, and lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender employees.

Support

  • A range of ‘Family Friendly’ policies such as opportunities to work reduced hours or job share.
  • Access to flexible benefits such as voluntary benefits, retail vouchers and discounts on a range of goods and services.
  • For moves to or from another employer or moves across the Civil Service this can have implications on your eligibility to carry on claiming childcare vouchers. You may however be eligible for alternative government childcare support schemes, including Tax Free Childcare. More information can be found on or Childcare Choices. You can determine your eligibility at .
  • Paid paternity, adoption and maternity leave.
  • Free annual sight tests for employees who use computer screens.

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. Should you feel that the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you are able to raise a formal complaint in the following order

  • To Transformative Business Services (0345 241 5359 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or e mail moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@resourcing.soprasteria.co.uk);
  • To Ministry of Justice Resourcing team (resourcing-management-office@justice.gov.uk);
  • To the Civil Service Commission (details available here)

As a Disability Confident employer, MoJ are committed to providing everyone with the opportunity to demonstrate their skills, talent and abilities, by making adjustments throughout all elements of the recruitment process and in the workplace. MoJ are able to offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns.

For more information on applying for a role as a candidate with a disability or long-term condition, please watch our animated videos.

You will be able to request reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process within the application form. If you need additional help completing the application form, please contact the TBS Recruitment Enquiries Team.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.

A Great Place to Work for Veterans

The "Making the Civil Service a Great Place to work for veterans" initiative includes a guaranteed interview scheme to those who meet the minimum criteria to provide eligible former members of the Armed Forces with opportunities to secure rewarding jobs. Allowing veterans to continue to serve their country, and to bring highly skilled individuals with a broad range of experience into the Civil Service in an environment, which recognises and values your previous service in the Armed Forces.
For further details about the initiative and eligibility requirements visit:

Redeployment Interview Scheme

Civil Service departments are expected to explore redeployment opportunities before making an individual redundant. The MoJ is committed, as part of the Redeployment Interview Scheme, to providing opportunities to those who are 'at risk of redundancy'.

MoJ is able to offer an interview to eligible candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns. Candidates will not be eligible for the Redeployment Interview Scheme if they are applying on promotion.

title: Assistant Emergency Planning Officer
description:
Salary £29,071 - £33,119 per annum | Permanent, Full Time 37 hours per week | Preston

Please note that we are unable to offer sponsorship for this role

Help Lancashire prepare for emergencies

Lancashire County Council’s Resilience Team helps ensure the council is ready to respond when emergencies affect our communities or the services they rely on.

We work closely with emergency services, councils and other partner organisations to plan for emergencies, test our arrangements and support the response and recovery when incidents happen.

We are looking for an Assistant Emergency Planning Officer to join the team. This is a great opportunity for someone who is organised, curious and a strong communicator to build a career in emergency planning and resilience.

You do not need to already be an emergency planning professional. We are interested in the skills and experience you can bring to the role and your ability to learn and develop.

The role

No two days in emergency planning are quite the same. You could be helping review an emergency plan, organising a multi-agency exercise, researching an emerging risk or supporting the council during a live incident.

You will manage your own areas of work while being part of an experienced team, using judgement and initiative to analyse information, solve problems and deliver work to agreed standards and deadlines.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Support the development and maintenance of emergency plans, procedures and operational information.
  • Helping to plan and deliver emergency training and exercises.
  • Supporting the Council’s response to and recovery from emergencies.
  • Working with colleagues and partner organisations to strengthen emergency preparedness.
  • Researching and analysing information and turning it into clear plans, briefings and reports.
  • Coordinating your own areas of work, actions and priorities

What we are looking for

You don't necessarily need previous emergency planning experience. We are looking for someone with the ability and potential to develop within the profession.

You will need to be:

  • A strong communicator who can build effective working relationships with different people and organisations.
  • Organised and able to prioritise, including when circumstances or priorities change.
  • A good writer and problem solver, able to understand information, identify what matters and communicate it clearly.
  • Confident with technology, including Microsoft 365, and comfortable learning new systems and ways of working.
  • Able to use your own initiative, manage your workload and know when to seek advice.

Experience or qualifications in emergency planning, resilience, business continuity, risk management or a related area would be an advantage, but are not essential.

Working in emergency planning

Emergencies don't always happen during normal working hours. You will need to be willing to support the Council's response to emergencies when required, which may include working outside normal hours.

The role also involves working with organisations across Lancashire, so you will need to be able to travel across the county when required.

In return, you will have the opportunity to develop your knowledge and experience across emergency planning, training and exercising, multi-agency working, response and recovery.

You'll be joining a team where you'll be supported to develop your professional knowledge and take on greater responsibility as your experience grows.

Why join us?

This is an opportunity to build a career in an area of work that makes a real difference to Lancashire's communities.

You'll gain experience of working with a wide range of services and partner organisations and contribute directly to Lancashire's preparedness for emergencies.

Lancashire County Council also offers a range of employee benefits, including a local government pension and annual leave entitlement.

Interested?

If you'd like an informal discussion about the role, please contact:

Kevin Topping, Emergency Planning Manager, 01772 533396 kevin.topping@lancashire.gov.uk

Applications are welcomed from people with transferable skills as well as those who already have experience in emergency planning or resilience.

Closing Date: 22/11/2026 Interview Date: w/c 07/12/2026

We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications.

Local Government Reorganisation

The Government has confirmed that local government across Lancashire will be reorganised, with the current 15 councils being replaced by four new unitary councils covering North, South, East and West Lancashire from April 2028.

If you are successful in your application, you will initially join Lancashire County Council. However, as part of the planned transition, your employment will transfer to one of the new unitary councils from April 2028, subject to the implementation of the reorganisation and relevant employment legislation.

Throughout this period, our focus remains on delivering excellent services to our communities. By joining us now, you'll play an important role in shaping the future of local government and helping to build a strong new organisation that will serve residents for years to come.

title: Claim Director
description:
This is a role focused on technical claim handling for Westchester insured’s nationwide. In this role you will manage complex excess casualty, both litigated and non-litigated. This role requires an individual to be accountable for the handling and disposition of claims including investigation, coverage determination, reserving, negotiation and settlement or trial strategies. This position will require some travel, as well as coordinating with and servicing both internal and external business partners. You will represent the company at meetings with management and business partners, as well as at mediations, arbitrations, settlement conferences and trials.

Responsibilities

  • Provides outstanding customer service and works well with the insured and broker in the adjustment of mainstream casualty, specialty risks, and business auto claims.
  • Analyzes coverage and communicates coverage positions, as warranted, under direction of supervisor and coverage unit.
  • Conducts, coordinates, and directs investigation into loss facts and extent of third-party damages.
  • Directs and closely monitors assignments to experts and defense counsel.
  • Evaluates information on coverage, liability, and damages to determine the extent of exposure to the insured and the company.
  • Sets reserves within authority or makes claim recommendations concerning reserve changes to supervisor.
  • Travels to conferences, mediations, and trials as necessary. Travel ranges from approximately 10% to 20%, but it could be more as dictated by business needs.

Who are we looking for?

Successful professionals at Chubb come from many backgrounds and experiences and bring that rich diversity with them to our company along with:

  • an inclusive mindset which allows differences to be leveraged for better business results;
  • open, transparent communication;
  • teamwork and inclusion which draws on diverse ideas and perspectives; and
  • new ideas, innovation, and ways of thinking which support diversity.

Qualifications

  • 3 - 5 experience as a claims professional or attorney with a high degree of specialized and technical competence in the handling of high exposure claims with emphasis on hands-on file and litigation management.
  • Automobile and General Liability (GL) experience in Products, Premises Liability, Oil / Gas and Energy, Trucking, and Advertising Injury claims.
  • Strong background and demonstrated ability in dealing with significant coverage matters, including Additional Insured analyses.
  • An understanding of the tenants of insurance and legal principles.
  • Knowledge of Property & Casualty Group coverage and services.
  • Working knowledge of industry best practices and procedures.
  • An ability to work independently and assimilate learning materials on many different subjects from various sources.
  • Excellent interpersonal communications and negotiation skills; and an ability to deal with customers and business partners in a professional manner.
  • Ability to make prompt, intelligent decisions based upon detailed analysis of complex issues.
  • Demonstrated strong relational skills particularly in adverse or high-pressure situations.
  • A law degree is not necessary but recommended.

If you do not already have one, you will be required to obtain an applicable resident or designated home state adjusters license and possibly additional state licensure.

The pay range for the role is $83,600 to $119,900. The specific offer will depend on an applicant’s skills and other factors. This role may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. Chubb offers a comprehensive benefits package, more details on which can be found on our careers website. The disclosed pay range estimate may be adjusted for the applicable geographic differential for the location in which the position is filled.

title: 23922 - Engineer Geotechnical
description:
Perform or monitor geotechnical investigations and testing. Perform pavement and geotechnical plan reviews and designs. Prepare analyses, reports and recommendations on geotechnical findings. Provide geotechnical engineering support and consultation for preliminary engineering, construction and maintenance activities. Provide technical advice, guidance and training regarding assigned engineering program areas. Prepare analyses, reports, and recommendations based on engineering determinations. Provide engineering support and consultation related to engineering program area. Effectively manage assigned projects to ensure timely and accurate completion. Communicate with internal VDOT staff, local government staff, consultants, citizens and FHWA regarding transportation projects and programs.

How you will contribute:
  • Analysis and Technical Reporting: Analyze and interpret engineering data and information. Prepare complete, clear and concise reports and recommendations.
  • Analysis and Technical Reporting: Analyze and interpret information and data obtained during preliminary engineering and special investigations. Prepare complete, clear and concise reports and recommendations for soil surveys, pavement designs, major and minor structures, well and vibration damage assessments, slope failures, etc. Work with Central Office to produce special designs and recommendations requiring engineering expertise.
  • Communication: Establish an effective line of communication between VDOT, contractors, government agencies and the public. Investigate issues and resolve complaints.
  • Engineering Process Management: Use established VDOT policies and procedures in the development and delivery of engineering projects. Engineering projects are completed in compliance with state and federal laws and regulations.
  • Manage Assigned Activities: Plan, schedule and coordinate engineering program activities such that deliverables are met within the established scope and timeline.
  • On-Call Contracts: May administer geotechnical on-call contracts for geotechnical services and drilling activities. Investigate projects and locate boreholes for soil surveys and foundation investigations. Prepare scope of work and request for proposal documents and issues notice to proceed based on agreed services between consultant and VDOT. Verify consultant work is acceptable and required information is received.
  • Preliminary Engineering Investigations: Plan, schedule and coordinate activities with the drill crew or consultant services for soil surveys and foundation investigations.
