title: Head of Information Security
description:
Mercury is the European leader in construction solutions.

We build and manage complex engineering & construction projects for the world’s leading corporations. Our solutions help deliver technologies and life changing advancements that connect people, communities, and businesses, giving them the power to achieve incredible things. Our people have the courage to be innovative. Their determination and sharp focus enable us to deliver with certainty, time and time again.

We deliver our clients’ visions through leading edge construction solutions across multiple sectors, including Enterprise Data Centres, Advanced Technology & Life Sciences, Hyperscale Data Centres, Fire Protection.

At Mercury, it is our duty to encourage and back our people to realise their vision of themselves. We place them at the heart of what we do, providing challenging opportunities to develop within a great team in a supportive environment that allows them to reach their full potential.

Scope of the Role:

We are seeking a Head of Information Security to own and lead the information security function for Mercury Engineering. Reporting to the Head of IT, the successful candidate will set the direction of our security, compliance and third-party risk agenda, and translate it into a funded, measurable programme of work.

This is a strategic leadership role rather than a hands-on operations role. The Head of Information Security is accountable for the overall security posture of the organisation: the design and maintenance of the information security management system, the way security risk is identified, quantified and reported to senior leadership, the assurance we provide to clients, and the management of security risk introduced through our supply chain and joint venture partners. Day-to-day monitoring and response activity is delivered through internal specialists and managed security service providers, whom this role directs and holds to account.

The role carries influence well beyond the IT function. The successful candidate will be expected to engage credibly with executive leadership, client security teams, auditors, insurers and Tier 1 suppliers, and to represent Mercury’s security position in commercial and contractual discussions.

Key Responsibilities of the Role:

Security Strategy and Governance

  • Security strategy: Define, own and maintain a multi-year information security strategy and roadmap aligned to Mercury’s business plan, client commitments and risk appetite. Secure senior leadership endorsement and review the strategy at least annually.
  • Governance framework: Own the information security policy framework, standards and supporting procedures. Ensure they remain current, proportionate, understood by the business, and consistent with the requirements of the sectors we build in.
  • Executive and board reporting: Produce and present clear reporting on security posture, risk, incidents and programme delivery to the Head of IT, executive leadership and relevant committees. Translate technical exposure into commercial and operational terms.
  • Assurance and control effectiveness: Establish a control assurance approach that evidences whether controls are operating as designed, using a combination of internal testing, independent assessment and audit.
  • Metrics: Define and report a meaningful set of security and compliance metrics, and use them to direct investment and prioritisation rather than simply to describe activity.

Information Security Risk Management

  • Risk framework: Own the information security risk management methodology, risk register and treatment planning. Ensure security risk is captured, owned by the business and escalated consistently with Mercury’s wider enterprise risk process.
  • Risk assessment: Direct regular risk assessments across the corporate estate, project environments and site-based technology. Ensure findings translate into funded, tracked remediation with clear ownership.
  • Risk acceptance: Advise business owners on residual risk, articulate options and consequences clearly, and administer a defensible exception and risk acceptance process.
  • Emerging risk: Maintain awareness of the threat landscape relevant to construction and to our clients’ sectors, and of emerging risk areas such as artificial intelligence adoption, operational technology on site, and cloud concentration.

Compliance and Certification

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022: Act as the senior owner of the information security management system. Maintain and continually improve the ISMS, direct internal audit and management review, own the corrective action process, and lead preparation for and engagement with the certification body across surveillance and recertification audits.
  • Scope management: Manage the certified scope of the ISMS, including changes arising from new business, new locations, acquisitions and changes to service delivery models.
  • Regulatory compliance: Maintain oversight of information security obligations arising from applicable law and regulation, including data protection legislation and network and information security requirements, working with Legal, Data Protection and Compliance colleagues to ensure obligations are met and evidenced.
  • Contractual compliance: Ensure security commitments given to clients are understood, achievable and demonstrably met, and that gaps are identified before they become findings.
  • Frameworks and benchmarking: Assess Mercury’s posture against recognised frameworks and client-mandated standards, and use the results to prioritise improvement.

Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk

  • Programme ownership: Design, implement and own a third-party information security risk management programme covering suppliers, subcontractors, joint venture partners, agency labour providers and technology vendors.
  • Due diligence: Establish risk-based due diligence and tiering for new and existing third parties, and lead assessment of Tier 1 relationships personally.
  • Contractual controls: Work with Procurement, Legal and Commercial to embed appropriate security, confidentiality, incident notification, audit and data handling obligations in contracts, pre-qualification and tender documentation.
  • Ongoing monitoring: Maintain continuous oversight of third-party security performance, including periodic reassessment, remediation tracking, and escalation where a supplier’s posture presents unacceptable risk to Mercury or our clients.
  • Site and project supply chain: Address the specific characteristics of construction supply chains, including short-notice mobilisation, transient workforces, shared site environments and client-imposed security requirements on subcontractors.
  • Fourth-party and concentration risk: Understand and report on material dependencies held by our key suppliers, and on concentration risk within critical services.

Security Operations Oversight

  • Service provider governance: Own the relationship with managed security service providers delivering managed detection and response, endpoint protection and vulnerability management as a service. Set expectations, govern performance against service levels, review outputs critically and drive continual improvement.
  • Operational direction: Direct the internal security team in the delivery of monitoring, vulnerability management, identity and access governance, and security tooling administration, ensuring priorities reflect assessed risk.
  • Security architecture: Provide security input and approval into technology change, infrastructure design, cloud adoption and project delivery, working with infrastructure and applications colleagues to embed security by design.
  • Vulnerability and patch assurance: Set standards for vulnerability identification and remediation across the estate, and hold technical owners to account for closure within agreed timeframes.

Incident Response and Resilience

  • Incident management: Own the security incident response framework. Lead the response to significant security incidents, including containment decisions, internal and external communications, regulatory and client notification, investigation and post-incident review.
  • Preparedness: Run regular exercises and simulations with technical teams and senior leadership so that response capability is tested rather than assumed.
  • Resilience: Contribute security requirements to business continuity and disaster recovery planning, and assure the recoverability of critical systems and data.
  • External engagement: Maintain appropriate relationships with law enforcement, national cyber authorities, insurers and specialist response providers, and coordinate with them when required.

Security Culture and Awareness

  • Awareness programme: Own the company-wide security awareness and training programme, including phishing simulation, role-based training and onboarding, and measure its effect on behaviour rather than completion rates alone.
  • Senior engagement: Convene security workshops and briefings with senior stakeholders and project leadership to build understanding of risk and ownership of controls.
  • Site and project engagement: Extend security awareness to project and site-based teams, recognising that they operate in client environments with their own requirements and constraints.

Leadership, People and Budget

  • Team leadership: Lead, develop and structure the information security team. Set objectives, manage performance, identify capability gaps and build a succession and development plan.
  • Resourcing: Determine the appropriate balance between internal capability and outsourced service, and make the case for resourcing where required.
  • Budget ownership: Own the information security budget, including multi-year forecasting, business case development, procurement and management of spend against plan.
  • Commercial engagement: Support bids, tenders and client onboarding by providing security content, completing client security assessments, and participating in client audits and due diligence.

Essential Criteria for the Role:

  • Experience: Minimum of 10 years’ experience in information security, of which at least 4 years in a leadership role with accountability for strategy, budget and team.
  • Governance and compliance: Demonstrable ownership of an ISO/IEC 27001 certified management system, including audit preparation, management review, corrective action and scope management. Working knowledge of the 2022 revision.
  • Risk management: Proven experience establishing and running an information security risk management framework in a distributed organisation, and reporting risk to executive audiences.
  • Third-party risk: Practical experience designing and operating a third-party or supply chain security risk programme, including due diligence, contractual controls and ongoing monitoring.
  • Technical grounding: Sound understanding of security architecture, identity and access management, cloud and Microsoft 365 security, network security, endpoint protection, detection and response, and vulnerability management — sufficient to direct specialists and challenge suppliers with authority.
  • Incident leadership: Experience leading the response to significant security incidents, including decision making under pressure and communication with senior stakeholders.
  • Supplier management: Experience managing managed security service providers and security vendors, including commercial negotiation and performance management.
  • Regulatory awareness: Working knowledge of data protection legislation and of the direction of network and information security regulation as it applies to organisations of Mercury’s size and sector.
  • Communication: Ability to present complex risk clearly and without exaggeration to non-technical audiences, and to write to a standard suitable for executive and client consumption.
  • Education: Primary degree in information technology, information security, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Certification: CISM, CISSP, CRISC, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer, or equivalent.
  • Sector experience: Experience in construction, engineering, or another project-based industry, or in serving clients in data centre, semiconductor or pharmaceutical sectors.
  • Client-facing assurance: Experience representing an organisation’s security posture to major clients, including participation in client-led audits.
  • Additional frameworks: Familiarity with NIS2, CIS Controls, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, SOC 2 or client-specific security standards.
  • Multi-jurisdiction: Experience operating a security function across multiple European jurisdictions.
  • Postgraduate study: Master’s degree in information security, risk management or a related field.

title: Global Regulatory Strategy Director
description:
Let’s build the future of medicine - together.

Remote | Full-Time | $220,000 - $250,000

YOUR ROLE

As a Global Regulatory Strategy Director at Enveda, you'll lead the development and execution of innovative regulatory strategies for our pipeline of first-in-class small-molecule medicines. You'll partner with global project teams as the regulatory subject matter expert and lead Enveda's interactions with health authorities worldwide. In your first year, you'll shape our global registrational strategies and lead the submissions that support them. This is a high impact opportunity where you'll influence our global regulatory strategy and small-molecule clinical pipeline while collaborating with some of the brightest minds in the industry.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Provide regulatory leadership for Enveda's assets through Phase 2 and beyond, and lead the development of global registrational strategies
  • With minimal supervision, develop innovative global regulatory strategies for Enveda's portfolio in clinical development and life-cycle management
  • Lead the development of regulatory submissions (INDs, CTx, briefing documents, IB, NDA, DMF, IMPD, and more), identifying gaps and developing risk mitigation strategies
  • Represent Enveda with global health authorities and lead agency interactions to achieve company objectives
  • Represent Regulatory Affairs on cross-functional teams as the subject matter expert, providing regulatory guidance and oversight to global project teams
  • Ensure Enveda's regulatory activities comply with health authority requirements, and coordinate and maintain all HA reporting schedules with cross-functional teams
  • Stay on top of the regulatory landscape and keep leadership informed of health authority initiatives and their impact on Enveda's programs
  • Lead the global regulatory team(s), mentor and develop regulatory colleagues, and support Regulatory Affairs senior leadership as needed
  • Lead the development of Regulatory Affairs policies, SOPs, and work instructions, and guide cross-functional teams on AI implementation for regulatory dossiers

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline; an advanced degree (MS, PharmD, or PhD) is preferred
  • At least 12 years of Regulatory Affairs experience in pharma or biotech; experience across all phases of development is highly preferred
  • Strong negotiation skills with health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA, Health Canada), plus submission experience from IND/CTx through NDA or marketing applications
  • Experience developing and executing regulatory strategies for oral small-molecule programs, and experience in obesity or dermatology, both strongly preferred
  • Excellent oral, written, and presentation skills, including experience presenting to leadership teams
  • Demonstrated organizational awareness, including experience representing Regulatory Affairs cross-functionally and on global teams
  • Excellent planning and organizational skills, with the ability to work on multiple projects with tight timelines in a fast-paced, hands-on environment
  • Strong understanding of regulatory operational activities
  • Self-starter with an entrepreneurial spirit, flexible and proactive in adapting to changing business needs and priorities
  • Pragmatic, compliant, solution-oriented mindset

We hire for trajectory, not just credentials. If you meet most of the above and care deeply about this problem, we want to hear from you.

ABOUT ENVEDA

We're a clinical-stage, AI-enabled biotech discovering medicines from nature four times faster than the industry standard. title: Real Estate Transaction Manager
description:
Position Summary

The Real Estate Transaction Manager manages Pike's real estate transactions from the initial space request through lease execution and ongoing administration. This role serves Pike business units as their primary point of contact for leasing activity, works with outside brokers, landlords and legal counsel, and keeps the real estate portfolio data accurate and ready for reporting. The Transaction Manager works independently on most deals and escalates complex or strategic matters to the Senior Director of Real Estate. This is a fully on-site role in our Uptown Charlotte, NC office.

Essential Functions:

Transaction Management

  • Manage lease transactions end to end, including new leases, renewals, expansions, contractions, amendments, subleases, assignments and terminations.

  • Prepare and negotiate letters of intent, proposals and lease business terms in line with each business unit's needs and Pike's goals.

  • Analyze and compare proposals, including net effective rent, total occupancy cost and lease-versus-alternative scenarios.

  • Coordinate lease drafts and amendments with Legal and confirm that agreed business terms are reflected in the final documents.

  • Track lease critical dates, including expirations, renewal and termination notice deadlines and rent escalations, and act on them well ahead of time.

Stakeholder and Broker Management

  • Engage and manage outside brokers, landlords, attorneys and other third-party providers as needed.

  • Give regular transaction status updates to the Senior Director of Real Estate and business unit leaders by email, in meetings and on calls.

Portfolio Administration and Reporting

  • Update the real estate portfolio database, including locations, square footage, seats, lease terms and occupancy costs.

  • Prepare data, Excel analyses and PowerPoint materials for the quarterly business review and other leadership reporting.

  • Work with Accounting and Risk on lease accounting inputs, insurance requirements, security deposits and landlord documentation.

  • Keep complete, organized lease files and transaction records.

Workplace Planning and Process Improvement

  • Support space planning and workplace initiatives that reduce vacancy, wasted rent and capital spend, and identify consolidation or disposition opportunities.

  • Document transaction processes and maintain templates, checklists and standard workflows that improve consistency and speed.

Minimum Requirements:

  • 3+ years of commercial real estate transactions on the corporate, brokerage or landlord side.

  • 4-year degree in business, real estate, or finance.

  • A valid North Carolina real estate broker license, or agreement to obtain one within a defined period after hire.

  • Working knowledge of commercial lease structures, lease terms and negotiation practices.

  • Strong Excel skills for financial analysis, and proficiency with PowerPoint and Word.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to manage several transactions at once while meeting deadlines.

  • High attention to detail and quality across all deliverables.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with lease administration or CRE software and with CoStar or similar market data tools.

  • Professional real estate designation, such as CCIM.

  • Experience supporting a multi-business-unit or multi-site corporate portfolio.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands and fingers to handle, feel, or operate objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms.

Work Environment:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions (such as in typical office or administrative work). This role will require periodic travel to Pike locations and markets for site visits, tours and meetings.

Our Benefits:

  • Medical, dental and vision insurance

  • HSA, dependent care and medical flexible spending accounts

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Life insurance, and short-term and long-term disability

  • Paid time off, paid holidays, and family and medical leave

If this sounds like you, come join the PIKE family.

About Us

Founded in 1945, Pike is a leading provider of construction, repair and engineering services for electric and gas utilities, as well as telecommunications companies with a growing portfolio of turnkey renewable projects. We work with hundreds of utility clients across the country, and we continuously expand our offerings to supply our customers with the ideas, technology, experience, workforce and equipment to perform any job.

"Essential" is the one word that sums up who we are, the work we do and what our people mean to us. Each of our employees plays a critical role in ensuring that infrastructure systems are up and running when people and businesses need them.

Pike is a family-oriented workplace with a strong culture of safety, collaboration, innovation and exceptional customer service.

Equal Employment Opportunity

title: Data Engineer | Bli med å bygge fremtidens dataløsninger i et av Norges største inhouse tech-miljøer
description:
I SpareBank 1 Utvikling gir vi over én million personer, bedrifter og lokalsamfunn over hele landet trygghet, forutsigbarhet og nærhet til økonomien deres gjennom teknologi som begeistrer. Vi er SpareBank 1-alliansens viktigste forretningspartner og en spydspiss innen teknologiutvikling. Nesten 500 dyktige medarbeidere og en rekke konsulenter jobber med alt fra utvikling, sikkerhet, drift, innkjøp, merkevare og mye annet spennende. Hos oss danner samarbeid, kompetanse, deling og tillit grunnmuren i arbeidshverdagen - dette gjør SpareBank 1 Utvikling til et spennende sted å jobbe og et godt sted å være!

Som den viktigste teknologipartneren i SpareBank 1-alliansen leverer vi mobilbank, infrastruktur og datatjenester som gir over én million brukere og bedrifter trygghet og forutsigbarhet. Vi brenner for å ta i bruk kraften i data for å skape gode opplevelser for bankene og produktselskapene våre. Nå skalerer vi opp satsingen og søker fem data engineers som vil være med å forme datalandskapet, arkitekturen og verktøyene våre fremover.

I SpareBank 1 Utvikling er vi bankenes og produktselskapenes viktigste teknologipartner. Vi utvikler alt fra mobilbank og infrastruktur til avanserte plattformtjenester. Hos oss blir du en del av Data og Innsikt – et miljø på rundt 35 dyktige data engineers, data plattform engineers, data analyster og data scientister som jobber inn i tverrfaglige team og deler kunnskap, sparrer og løser komplekse utfordringer sammen.

Hva gjør oss annerledes enn andre arbeidsplasser?

  • Fagtid: Vi setter av tid til egenutvikling, eksperimentering og kompetansedeling. Hos oss er kontinuerlig læring en del av driftshverdagen, ikke noe du må skvise inn på kveldstid.
  • Mennesket og samarbeidet i sentrum: Vi tror på at de beste løsningene skapes sammen. Vi bruker blant annet parjobbing for å dele innsikt, gjøre opplæringen trygg og heve kvaliteten på koden.
  • Inhouse med ekte påvirkningskraft: Du får stor frihet til å forme arkitekturen og bidra inn i moderniseringen og forvaltning av nye dataprodukter.
  • Stor skala, men nærhet til brukeren: Du får bryne deg på datamengder i toppklassen i norsk målestokk, samtidig som samfunnsoppdraget vårt er merkbart: Trygghet og god økonomisk oversikt for folk over hele landet.
  • Vi eksperimenterer og tilpasser oss: Vi er nysgjerrige på moderne arbeidsmetodikker. I det siste har vi eksperimentert med parjobbing på dataområdet. Dette kan du lese mer om her: Kan man parprogrammere på dataområdet? | by Ruben Gudmundsrud | SpareBank 1 Utvikling | Oct, 2026 | Medium


Hvordan vil hverdagen din se ut?

Som Data Engineer hos oss blir du en nøkkelspiller i oppbyggingen og videreutviklingen av vår skybaserte data- og analyseplattform – selve fundamentet for innsikt, modellering og beslutninger i alliansen.

Du vil blant annet:

  • Utvikle og forvalte robuste, skalerbare dataprodukter og pipelines i skyen.
  • Automatisere og optimalisere dataintegrasjoner og ETL-prosesser.
  • Jobbe med moderne verktøy som Snowflake, dbt og Python.
  • Samarbeide tett i tverrfaglige team for å skape reell verdi.


Hvem trives hos oss?

Vi ser etter deg som er nysgjerrig, strukturert og trives i et miljø der man støtter hverandre. Du motiveres av å bygge smidige løsninger som gjør hverdagen enklere for andre, og du liker å bryne deg på data i stor skala.

Det er en fordel om du har erfaring med:

  • SQL, datamodellering og ETL/ELT-prosesser.
  • dbt eller tilsvarende moderne transformasjonsverktøy.

Ingen kan alt, og det forventer vi heller ikke. Vi legger største vekt på din læringsvilje, hvordan du samarbeider, og din evne til å sette deg inn i nye problemstillinger. Om du kjenner deg igjen i mesteparten av det som står over, vil vi veldig gjerne høre fra deg!


Hva tilbyr vi deg?

  • Fast ansettelse i et raust, trygt og sterkt fagmiljø.
  • Vi har avsatt tid til kompetanseheving i arbeidstiden, også kjent som fagtid
  • Konkurransedyktige betingelser, samt gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger.
  • Fine lokaler midt i Oslo sentrum med treningsrom, hyggelige sosiale soner og sommertid.
  • En bedriftskultur som verdsetter balanse mellom jobb og fritid.


Nysgjerrig? Søk da vel!

Dersom du ønsker å bli litt mer kjent med oss eller stillingen før du søker, eller hvis du har noen spørsmål, er du hjertelig velkommen til å ta kontakt med Ruben Gudmundsrud, seksjonsleder Data og Innsikt, på 47337376 eller ruben.gudmundsrud@sparebank1.no.

Du kan også lære mer om hvem vi er og hvordan vi jobber på karieresiden vår eller på LinkedIn, Instagram eller Medium!

Hos oss er det enkelt å søke - du trenger bare å laste opp en CV og skrive noen ord om hvorfor du ønsker å jobbe hos oss. Vi ønsker å fortsette å representere mangfoldet i den norske befolkningen, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke på stillingen.

Vi anbefaler at du er tidlig ute med å søke da vi kjører løpende vurderinger til denne stillingen.

I SpareBank 1 Utvikling har vi norsk som arbeidsspråk – gode norskkunnskaper er derfor en forutsetning for å kunne jobbe hos oss.

I forkant av ansettelse gjennomføres en bakgrunnssjekk for å blant annet verifisereopplysninger som kommer frem av CV og tilgjengelig dokumentasjon. Stillingen vurderes som kritisk og det vil også gjennomføres en Sårbarhetssamtale i forkant av ansettelsen. Bakgrunnssjekk gjennomføres av Semac AS etter at kandidat er orientert om og har godkjent det.

title: Assistant Steam Distribution Operator - Facilities & Services
description: Duties & Responsibilities Assist in the operation and/or investigation/inspection of valves, traps, pumps, PRV’s expansion joints, piping, supports, tunnels, entries, insulation, lighting, etc. on the campus steam distribution and condensate return system. Assist in operation and/or inspection/investigation of natural gas transmission and distribution systems, valves, piping, supports, regulator stations, and associated equipment. Assist in the operation and adjustment of PRV stations for building heating systems. Turn heating, ventilating and air conditioning systems on or off in accordance with operating schedules, and conditions at Abbott Power Plant. Operate systems to avoid damage to Abbott Power Plant equipment. In building equipment rooms and tunnels: check for cleanliness, clean as directed, check condensate return pumps for proper operation and normal condensate temperature, discharge pressure and vacuum; check condensate meters, sump pumps, ventilation, lighting and security for proper operation. Check temperature controls on heating, ventilating and air conditioning systems to be sure proper conditions are being maintained in the most efficient manner. Check ventilating and exhaust fan units for proper operation of components: motors, bearings, fans, heating and cooling coils, dampers, ductwork, valves, traps and controls. Check the condition of coils, ductwork, dampers, louvers, grilles, etc., for damage and cleanliness. Clean that which is Steam Distribution responsibility as directed. Report damage to supervision. The operation of isolated heating plants as directed by supervision. Maintaining proper temperatures, checking boilers and furnaces, inspecting controls, support equipment and reporting needed maintenance or repair. Maintain an operating log as directed. Report all malfunctions or need for repairs to supervision so service requests can be initiated. Periodic inspection of ventilation system filters. Determine when filters need to be cleaned or replaced, and report to supervision as directed. Periodic inspection and/or lubrication of all grease and oil bearing on mechanical equipment, including sump pump motor bearings in tunnels, valves and expansion joints as directed. Motor bearings, except as noted, will be lubricated by others. Scheduled inspection of sewage lift stations. Assist in scheduled outages as directed by supervision. Record monthly utility meter readings as directed utilizing automated reading devices. Serve as campus eyes and ears during evenings, weekends, and holidays to check out, identify, and investigate off normal conditions, and if necessary, call for appropriate craft to take corrective action. As 2nd and 3rd year Assistant Steam Distribution Operator may perform locating service for campus steam distribution system, natural gas distribution system, and other utilities as assigned. Other duties as assigned. May be required to drive university vehicles.

title: Help Desk Specialist
description:
Empower your Future at One of the Nation’s Leading Independent Electrical Distributors!

At U.S. Electrical Services, Inc. As a family of 14 regional businesses, we thrive on innovation and teamwork, empowering our people to shape the future of the electrical industry.

Position Overview:

The IT Help Desk Specialist provides advanced technical support, independently manages assigned projects, and works directly with stakeholders, vendors, and IT teams. This hands-on position requires 5+ years of relevant IT support experience. Core technologies include Windows 11, Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Intune, Windows Autopilot, and Axis IP cameras. The specialist supports onsite and remote users while helping modernize endpoint deployment and management.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide Level 2 and Level 3 support for USESI business applications, Microsoft 365 applications including Outlook, computers, printers, peripherals, and network connectivity.
  • Diagnose hardware, software, and connectivity issues using monitoring tools, remote management applications, and available technical resources. Restore services and escalate urgent or complex incidents to the appropriate teams.
  • Guide Tier 1 and Tier 2 staff through troubleshooting, apply critical thinking to undocumented issues, and perform root cause analysis to reduce recurring problems.
  • Maintain clear communication and follow-up until incidents and requests are resolved. Build trust through professional, customer-focused support and meet established service targets and SLAs.
  • Record incidents, service requests, troubleshooting steps, and resolutions in Jira Service Management. Maintain accurate support documentation and knowledge articles.
  • Follow established Service Desk processes for incident, request, change, release, and problem management.
  • Configure, deploy, and manage Windows endpoints using Microsoft Intune and Windows Autopilot. Support the transition from traditional desktop imaging to modern deployment methods.
  • Create, maintain, and troubleshoot Intune configuration profiles, compliance policies, application packages, and update policies in coordination with infrastructure and security teams.
  • Troubleshoot device enrollment, provisioning, policy synchronization, and application deployment issues for onsite and remote users.
  • Maintain device provisioning, deployment, and retirement procedures. Standardize device configurations and application assignments based on employee roles and business requirements.
  • Install, diagnose, repair, upgrade, and maintain supported computers and peripherals. Perform approved software upgrades and deployments, obtaining required authorization for new software.
  • Assist infrastructure teams with approved server upgrades and maintenance, following change procedures and obtaining required hardware approvals.
  • Collaborate with IT teams and vendors to evaluate technologies, conduct proofs of concept, and implement reliable solutions that meet business needs and industry best practices.
  • Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Axis IP cameras, including network connectivity, Power over Ethernet (PoE), firmware updates, and video management system integration. Resolve camera availability, image quality, recording, and remote viewing issues with network teams and vendors.
  • Maintain camera location and configuration records, and coordinate camera installation and replacement with onsite teams or vendors.
  • Additional Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Assist with the installation and deployment of routers, switches, and phones.
  • Assist with data migrations during projects and corporate acquisitions.
  • Assist with onsite evaluations of IT assets during corporate acquisitions.
  • Support scheduled weekend cutovers and installation of networking equipment for project work.
  • Travel to other USESI locations as needed to support projects, equipment deployments, acquisitions, and onsite troubleshooting. Travel may include overnight stays.
  • Participate in on-call coverage as assigned and respond to urgent IT issues outside normal business hours, including evenings and weekends.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Proficiency with supported Microsoft 365 applications, Windows endpoint operating systems, and desktop, laptop, and tablet hardware; familiarity with Windows Server environments relevant to assigned support duties.
  • Knowledge of Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and their roles in identity and device management, including integration with Microsoft Intune and Windows Autopilot.
  • Understanding of modern endpoint management throughout the device lifecycle, from enrollment and provisioning through configuration, compliance, updates, and retirement.
  • Advanced knowledge of LAN and wireless technologies is preferred. Working knowledge of IP video surveillance, PoE, and video management systems is required.
  • Strong customer service, communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and collaborate with people at all levels of the organization.
  • Familiarity with PowerShell scripting to automate deployment and support tasks is preferred.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment:

The duties below may be performed with or without reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities to enable performance of the essential functions of the position.

  • Regularly use a computer and related equipment for troubleshooting, documentation, and communication.

  • Lift, move, and position computers, monitors, printers, and related IT equipment, using assistance or handling equipment as needed.

title: Quality Assurance and Improvement Practitioner | Full time, Permanent | Preston (Hybrid Working)
description:
Salary £37,563–£42,123 | Full time, Permanent | Preston (Hybrid Working)
About the role...
This is an exciting opportunity to join Commissioning and Quality (Market) as a Quality Assurance and Improvement Practitioner, working across Lancashire’s commissioned adult social care market. You’ll play an important role in understanding and assuring the quality of commissioned services, working with providers, colleagues and partners to recognise good practice, identify emerging risks and support continuous improvement.
The Adults, Health and Wellbeing Quality Assurance and Improvement Framework provides the strategic foundation and you’ll bring together feedback, data and audit evidence with provider intelligence and people’s lived experience to understand quality, identify emerging risks and support proportionate action. The focus is on whether services and the improvements providers make are having a positive impact on people’s lives, not simply whether processes have been completed.
You’ll undertake planned and responsive provider reviews, visits and observations across designated adult social care markets, with activity prioritised according to risk, intelligence and service need. Through engagement with people who draw on care and support, unpaid carers, representatives and advocates, you’ll ensure their experiences, rights and outcomes inform your findings and recommendations.
Working constructively with providers, you’ll contribute to and lead allocated improvement activity, including Quality Performance Improvement Plans (QPIPs). You’ll balance support with appropriate challenge, recognise good practice, monitor progress and check that improvements are embedded and sustainable. You’ll also identify and escalate quality, safeguarding and service continuity risks through established arrangements. Alongside colleagues in Quality, Commissioning, Market Management, operational services and partner organisations, you’ll share evidence and learning to support improvements in individual services and across the wider commissioned care market.
We’re looking for professional curiosity, sound judgement and the ability to analyse evidence, build relationships and challenge constructively. You’ll need relevant experience in quality assurance, service improvement, commissioning, contract monitoring, regulation, adult safeguarding or operational practice within adult social care, health or a related field. Please see the person specification for the full essential requirements.

title: Certified Professional Coder (CPC)
description:
Adelfi Medical Billing Solutions is a fully remote revenue cycle management firm serving 65+ healthcare practices, mostly in New York and New Jersey. Our clients include ambulatory surgery centers and practices in orthopedics, podiatry, vascular surgery, neurosurgery, physical therapy, and chiropractic. We specialize in complex reimbursement, including out-of-network billing and IDR arbitration, where accurate coding directly drives results.

We’re looking for an experienced, detail-driven Certified Professional Coder to join our coding team. You’ll code surgical and office encounters accurately, keep claims moving through charge entry, and resolve front-end rejections before they become denials.

What You’ll Do

Coding

Code operative reports for surgical procedures, including orthopedic, podiatric, vascular, and spine cases, using CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10-CM.
Code office visits and E/M services using current guidelines based on medical decision-making or time.
Apply modifiers correctly, including 25, 59/XS, 51, 79, 78, RT/LT, TA–T9, and F1–FA, and follow NCCI edits, MUEs, and bundling rules.
Track surgical global periods and code post-op and unrelated services appropriately.
Assign ICD-10-CM codes to the highest level of specificity supported by documentation.
Query providers clearly and compliantly when documentation is incomplete, unclear, or doesn’t support the services billed.
Review provider-selected codes and flag discrepancies before claims are submitted.

Charge and Demographic Entry

Enter charges accurately in the practice management system, including CPT, diagnosis, modifiers, units, place of service, and rendering and referring providers.
Enter and update patient demographics and insurance information, and verify eligibility when needed.
Reconcile charges against surgery schedules and appointment lists so no services are missed.

Rejections and Claim Resolution

Work clearinghouse and payer rejections daily, correct errors, and resubmit claims promptly.
Research and resolve claim edits related to coding, modifiers, demographics, and payer requirements.
Support the AR and denials teams on coding-related denials, including corrected claims and coding appeal language.
Identify recurring coding and rejection trends and recommend fixes to prevent them.

Quality and Compliance

Support internal coding audits and help maintain accuracy standards.
Stay current on CPT, ICD-10-CM, HCPCS, CMS, and payer policy updates.
Support accurate code assignment for out-of-network and IDR claims, where coding accuracy is critical.
Follow HIPAA and compliance standards in all work.

Requirements

Current CPC credential through AAPC is required.
A minimum of 5 years of professional coding experience is required.
Strong experience coding operative reports and office visits.
Thorough knowledge of CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10-CM, modifiers, NCCI edits, and global surgical periods.
Experience with charge entry, demographic entry, and working clearinghouse and payer rejections.
Ability to write clear, compliant provider queries.
Highly accurate, organized, and able to meet daily productivity and quality standards.
Reliable internet and a quiet, private, HIPAA-compliant workspace.

Preferred

Specialty credentials such as COSC (orthopedic), CPCO, or CASCC.
Experience coding orthopedic, podiatry, vascular, spine, or ASC cases.
Experience in eClinicalWorks (ECW) or ModMed.
Experience working for a billing company with multiple clients.
Familiarity with out-of-network billing and the No Surprises Act.

What We Offer

$30–$35/hour, based on experience and credentials.
Medical, dental, and vision benefits.
401(k).
Paid time off.
Fully remote work.

To Apply

Submit your resume along with:

Your CPC credential number and expiration date.
A brief summary of your coding experience, including the specialties you’ve coded and your experience with operative reports.

Applicants without a current CPC credential and 5+ years of coding experience will not be considered.

title: Remote Operations Center Operator
description:
Position

Remote Operations Center Operator - ROC Operator I

Location

Bloomington, Minnesota - Remote Operations Center (on-site)

About Us

Geronimo Power develops, owns, and operates large-scale power and affiliated digital infrastructure projects throughout America's Heartland, including solar, wind, energy storage, and powered data parks. As a farmer-founded and community-focused business, Geronimo Power equips landowners and rural communities with sustainable revenue to ignite local economic growth. To learn more about Geronimo Power, visit www.geronimopower.com or follow the company on LinkedIn.

About This Role

Geronimo Power is seeking a ROC Operator to join the Remote Operations Center team. The ROC is the centralized monitoring and operational hub for utility-scale solar, wind, and battery energy storage system (BESS) assets across multiple North American energy markets. The operator monitors fleet performance, responds to alarms and abnormal conditions, performs authorized control actions, coordinates field activity, documents operational events, and supports applicable reliability, regulatory, market, safety, and company requirements.

This is a full-time, hourly position assigned to a 24/7 operating environment. The role requires 12-hour rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays. The selected candidate will enter the ROC Operator qualification program as an Operator In-Training and may qualify as a ROC Operator I after completing required training, assessments, simulations, observed shift requirements, and final management qualification review. The typical training period is 3 to 6 months; progression is based on successful qualification and is not automatic.

Responsibilities

Fleet Monitoring and Operations

  • Monitor solar, wind, BESS, and balance-of-plant systems through SCADA, EMS, and related operational platforms.
  • Maintain continuous awareness of fleet operating conditions and respond to alarms using approved procedures.
  • Perform only those remote-control actions, plant mode changes, curtailments, startups, shutdowns, and restoration activities authorized for the assigned qualification level.
  • Escalate non-routine, high-risk, first-time, or non-procedural conditions to qualified operators, engineering, field operations, or leadership.

Event Response and Coordination

  • Coordinate with field technicians, transmission operators, utilities, balancing authorities, and ISO/RTO personnel during operational events, within assigned authorization.
  • Support outage coordination, maintenance activities, approved switching evolutions, and restoration following equipment failures, communications outages, weather events, or grid disturbances.
  • Participate in emergency and abnormal operating condition response activities and follow established notification and escalation protocols.

Documentation and Compliance

  • Maintain accurate shift logs, event records, notifications, outage information, and other operational documentation.
  • Follow approved procedures, work instructions, communication standards, human performance tools, and control-room turnover practices.
  • Support compliance with applicable NERC, ISO/RTO, environmental, safety, records-retention, and company requirements.

Training and Continuous Improvement

  • Complete required classroom training, computer-based training, structured on-the-job training, task performance evaluations, simulations, examinations, and observed shift requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve procedures, alarm response, operational efficiency, and situational awareness.
  • Contribute to lessons learned and operating experience reviews following significant events.

What You’ll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Ability to learn and consistently apply technical procedures, operating standards, and escalation protocols.
  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, written communication, and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain attention to detail and situational awareness in a continuously monitored environment.
  • Computer proficiency and the ability to work across multiple applications and monitoring systems.
  • Ability to work 12-hour rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate degree or higher in Electrical Technology, Power Systems, Engineering Technology, Renewable Energy Technology, or a related field.
  • Utility, military, power generation, transmission, distribution, dispatch, control-room, or industrial process experience.
  • Experience operating utility-scale solar, wind, or battery storage facilities.
  • Familiarity with PJM, MISO, ERCOT, SPP, or other ISO/RTO operations.
  • Experience with OSI Monarch, Ignition, OSI PI, or similar operational platforms.
  • PJM Generation Certification; NERC System Operator Certification (RC, BT, BI, or TO); or FEMA ICS/NIMS training.

Success in This Role Looks Like

  • Safety-first and compliance-focused decision-making
  • Strong situational awareness and conservative operations
  • Accurate procedure use, documentation, and shift turnover
  • Timely escalation and clear communication
  • Ownership, accountability, teamwork, and continuous learning
  • Consistent use of human performance tools

What You’ll Get

  • Competitive compensation and performance-based incentives
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
  • Paid time off and holidays
  • Tuition assistance and ongoing professional development
  • Employee assistance program (EAP) and wellness resources
  • Pet insurance and employee discount programs

Pay Range for the posted level: $34.62 - $43.17 per hour plus target annual bonus opportunity of 10%. Upon completion of the ROC Operator I Qualification program, the candidate will also receive a 5% increase in base wages. Actual compensation may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, and demonstrated market-relevant expertise.

Our Commitment

Geronimo Power is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing workplace where employees feel valued, supported, and energized to do their best work. We believe strong teams and strong communities drive better outcomes.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants.

title: Assembly Specialist
description:
MUST HAVE PRIOR EXPERIENCE IN BOAT BUILDING/MANUFACTURING WITH DEMONSTRABLE ELECTRICAL COMPONTENT ASSEMBLY EXPERIENCE

Company Description

Everglades Boats is an industry leader in premium offshore fishing boats. Founded in 1997, Everglades provides the ultimate choice for discerning boat owners and knowledgeable big-water anglers. Everglades is a high-end, refined brand that makes a personal statement about the status and savvy of its owner by applying best-in-class fishing amenities, premium-grade materials, and a highly-refined fit and finish. Widely recognized and respected in the industry for its hull performance and ride, Everglades patented RAMPCAP hulls are found throughout its model lineup. Receiving numerous industry awards and an unparalleled reputation for superior performance, Everglades recruits and retains the best talent in the industry.

Job Description

The Electrical Wiring Specialist will have a strong background in marine electrical systems and a passion for producing high-quality work. As an Electrical Wiring Specialist, you will play a vital role in ensuring the safe and efficient operation of electrical systems within our boats, contributing to the overall quality and reliability of our products.

This team member will further specialize in installation of Yamaha and Mercury motors, Seakeepers, hardware components, bilge system, water, hydraulic & fuel fittings, hoses, tanks and connections.

Competencies

  • Install, maintain, and repair electrical systems in boats, including wiring, lighting, power distribution, navigation equipment, and communication systems.
  • Interpret and follow electrical schematics, blueprints, and technical manuals to ensure accurate installation and troubleshooting.
  • Collaborate with other members of the boat building team, including designers, engineers, and technicians, to integrate electrical systems seamlessly into boat designs.
  • Select appropriate electrical components, cables, and wiring based on the specifications of the boat and its intended use.
  • Safely handle and install marine batteries, chargers, inverters, and other power-related equipment.
  • Conduct thorough testing and quality checks on installed electrical systems to identify and resolve any issues or defects.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant electrical codes, safety standards, and regulations to guarantee the safety of occupants and the vessel's seaworthiness.
  • Participate in sea trials and tests to verify the proper functioning of electrical systems under real-world conditions.
  • Provide guidance and support to less experienced team members, fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends, new technologies, and best practices in marine electrical systems to contribute innovative ideas to the team.
  • Mechanical troubleshooting
  • Marine electrical installation
  • Engine diagnosis

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent; additional technical education or certification in marine electrical systems is a strong asset.
  • Proven experience as an Electrical Wiring Specialist in the boat building, marine, or related industry.
  • Solid understanding of marine electrical systems, including AC and DC systems, wiring techniques, and electrical components.
  • Proficiency in reading and interpreting electrical schematics, diagrams, and technical manuals.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot electrical issues effectively.
  • Familiarity with marine electrical codes and regulations, such as ABYC standards.
  • Detail-oriented with a focus on producing accurate and high-quality work.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and adapt to changing project requirements.
  • Physical ability to work in confined spaces, climb ladders, and lift heavy equipment when necessary.
  • Certified in Yamaha Power and components installation
  • Certified in Mercury Power and components installation
  • Certified in Seakeeper installation
  • Certified in generator systems installation
  • ABYC certified (preferred)
  • A minimum of two years’ experience in marine assembly is preferred

Responsibilities

  • Assembles motors and equipment to create a completed product
  • Assembles parts using blueprints and templates
  • Manually aligns parts for assembly and uses hoists when necessary
  • Completes electrical troubleshooting
  • Resolves assembly complexities as needed and communicates recommendations to Supervisor
  • Deciphers schematics and blueprints
  • Reads wiring specifications and diagrams
  • Electrical assembly of components such as motors, pumps, and switches
  • Maintains a clean, safe and organized work area
  • Follows quality standards
  • All other tasks as assigned

Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

  • Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements include eye protection, hearing protection, gloves, protective suits, dusts masks and respirators.
  • The employee is regularly required to be on their feet; occasionally required to sit; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. Constant use of hands/hand tools for assembly, fine manipulation, inspecting parts, and/or machine operating. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 15 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Employees must be able to work a 10-hour shift or more in one workday, including planned and unplanned overtime.
  • Exhibits ability to work cautiously but efficiently in potentially hazardous conditions.

Work Environment:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. The noise level in the work environment can be moderate to loud and is non-climate controlled.

Vi sørger for, at du/I bliver introduceret til arbejdet og oplært i brug af værktøjer og metoder, så du kommer godt fra start. Derudover får du tildelt en mentor, der under praktikforløbet vil guide, vejlede og støtte din udvikling ud fra din uddannelsesplan og kompetencer.

Du bliver en integreret del af vores tværfaglige team, som består af dygtige og engagerede medarbejdere. Vi arbejder med varierende opgaver f.eks.:

Der er tale om ulønnet praktik fra 8 uger op til 6 måneder med en arbejdstid på 30-37 timer om ugen som udgangspunkt. Der er mulighed for fleksible arbejdstider, og vi tager hensyn til studieaktiviteter.

title: SB BATCHER II
description:
About the Role:

The SB Batcher II plays a critical role in ensuring the accurate and efficient batching of materials or products within a manufacturing or processing environment. This position is responsible for preparing, measuring, and combining ingredients or components according to precise specifications to maintain product quality and consistency. The role requires close collaboration with production teams to meet daily output targets while adhering to safety and quality standards. The SB Batcher II will also monitor equipment performance and report any discrepancies or issues to supervisors to minimize downtime. Ultimately, this position contributes directly to the smooth operation of the production line and the delivery of high-quality products to customers.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Previous experience in a manufacturing or production environment, preferably in batching or material handling.
  • Basic math skills to accurately measure and calculate batch quantities.
  • Ability to follow detailed instructions and standard operating procedures.
  • Physical ability to stand for extended periods and lift materials as required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with automated batching systems or industrial equipment operation.
  • Familiarity with quality control standards and documentation practices.
  • Certification in workplace safety or related training.
  • Basic computer skills for data entry and record keeping.
  • Strong communication skills to effectively collaborate with team members.

Responsibilities:

  • Accurately measure and batch raw materials or components according to established formulas and production schedules.
  • Operate batching equipment safely and efficiently, ensuring all machinery is maintained and cleaned as required.
  • Monitor batch quality and consistency, making adjustments as necessary to meet product specifications.
  • Maintain detailed records of batch quantities, materials used, and any deviations from standard procedures.
  • Collaborate with production and quality control teams to troubleshoot issues and improve batching processes.
  • Adhere to all safety protocols and company policies to maintain a safe working environment.
  • Assist in inventory management by reporting material shortages or discrepancies to supervisors.

Skills:

The required skills enable the SB Batcher II to perform precise measurements and operate batching equipment safely, ensuring product quality and consistency. Attention to detail and the ability to follow complex instructions are essential for maintaining accurate batch records and adhering to production standards. Physical stamina and manual dexterity are important for handling materials and operating machinery throughout the workday. Preferred skills such as familiarity with automated systems and quality control enhance efficiency and support continuous improvement efforts. Effective communication and basic computer proficiency facilitate collaboration with team members and accurate documentation of batching activities.

title: Sr. Software Engineer (Core Policy)
location: College Park, MD | Columbus, OH | Boston, MA
description:
Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data.

The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity.

Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control.

For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production.

Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide.

  • Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments.
  • Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies.
  • Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures.
  • We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Immuta’s Core Policy Team builds the technologies that power Immuta’s platform, enabling customers to author, manage, and enforce complex data access policies across modern data ecosystems.

We develop systems that automate governance and privacy enforcement across leading cloud data platforms, including Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, and Starburst. We work across engineering, product, design, and other partner teams to solve complex technical problems, improve scalability and performance, and deliver maintainable software that creates meaningful value for customers.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Core Policy Team, you’ll design, build, and evolve scalable, high-performance features that power Immuta’s policy abstraction and enforcement capabilities. You’ll work across front-end and back-end systems to turn complex product and technical challenges into clear, maintainable solutions.

You’ll take ownership of complex projects and features from technical design through delivery, rollout, and follow-up improvements. You’ll contribute to architectural direction, use operational data to improve reliability and performance, and help create alignment across engineering and cross-functional partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role for an engineer who enjoys solving difficult problems, exercising technical judgment, and helping other engineers grow.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the design and end-to-end delivery of complex features and cross-component initiatives within the Core Policy Team, and when appropriate, across multiple engineering teams.
  • Design and implement maintainable front-end components using Angular, React, Vue.js, or comparable technologies.
  • Develop and evolve backend services, APIs, and data models using TypeScript, Node.js, and related technologies.
  • Create coherent designs across service, API, and data boundaries, anticipating failure modes, scalability needs, operational requirements, and long-term maintenance costs.
  • Improve the scalability, performance, reliability, and maintainability of existing systems through thoughtful refactoring, technical planning, and data-informed decisions.
  • Own quality through design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, observability, safe rollout practices, and clear success measures for the systems and features you deliver.
  • Partner with Product, Design, Security, and other Engineering teams to clarify requirements, evaluate tradeoffs, build alignment, and deliver cohesive solutions for customers.
  • Mentor engineers through thoughtful feedback, pairing, documentation, design discussions, and code reviews, helping raise technical standards and strengthen team practices.
  • Identify opportunities to improve engineering processes, tooling, CI/CD workflows, and developer experience, and follow through on improvements that increase team effectiveness.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • Experience: 5+ years in software engineering or a related discipline, with demonstrated scope and impact considered alongside tenure; preferred experience delivering production software.
  • Technical Skills: Strong proficiency in TypeScript and JavaScript, with experience building front-end applications using Angular, React, Vue.js, or comparable frameworks, and backend services using Node.js or related technologies.
  • Systems & Architecture: Experience designing and delivering services, APIs, and distributed systems with attention to scalability, maintainability, extensibility, reliability, and secure operation.
  • Data & APIs: Strong SQL and relational database fundamentals, including experience with PostgreSQL or comparable systems and designing data models and API contracts.
  • Engineering Quality: Experience with automated testing, code review, continuous integration and delivery, observability, debugging, and safe production rollouts.
  • Technical Judgment: Ability to frame ambiguous problems, consult the right stakeholders, evaluate tradeoffs, make timely decisions, and explain the rationale behind technical choices.
  • Project Ownership: Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects or cross-component initiatives from technical design through delivery, rollout, monitoring, and follow-up improvements.
  • Collaboration & Influence: Ability to build alignment and influence technical direction across Engineering and partner functions without relying on formal authority.
  • Leadership: Experience mentoring engineers, providing constructive feedback, and improving team practices through design reviews, documentation, code reviews, or other knowledge-sharing activities.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
BENEFITS

title: Product Counsel
description:
Mission: Help build the product legal foundation that lets Groq develop, launch, and scale next-generation AI infrastructure and applications quickly, responsibly, and with the trust of our customers.

The Team: Groq’s Legal team is a strategic partner across the business as we scale GroqCloud™ services and expand our AI infrastructure offerings across IaaS, PaaS, and AI applications. As Product Counsel, you will report to the Senior Director, Commercial & Product Legal, and work closely with Product, Engineering, AI, Security, and Commercial Legal. You will help build the product legal function at Groq from the ground up, designing the processes, policies, and frameworks that will guide how we launch and scale products. You’ll adapt industry best practices to the speed of a high-growth company, with mentorship and support from senior counsel.
The ideal candidate is a self-starter with real intellectual curiosity. You take feedback well, adapt quickly as priorities change, and do your best work in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

What You’ll Do:
  • Build the product review process. Design Groq’s intake, launch checklists, approval frameworks, and decision records. Scale industry best practices down so they fit how our engineers ship.
  • Counsel product teams from concept to launch. Work with Product and Engineering from early design onward to spot legal issues and give practical advice matched to the level of risk.
  • Advise across key regulatory areas. Cover product, privacy, AI, data, cybersecurity, and consumer protection law across our IaaS, PaaS, and future AI application offerings. Escalate novel or high-impact issues to senior counsel.
  • Keep the product and our commitments aligned. With Commercial Legal, make sure what the product does matches our customer commitments, contracting positions, disclosures, technical documentation, and marketing claims.
  • Own core product terms and policies. Draft and maintain our cloud service terms, SLAs, Acceptable Use Policy, Privacy Policy, and developer terms.
  • Support privacy and AI governance. Contribute to data mapping, privacy and AI risk assessments, shared responsibility models, and data residency.
  • Handle AI-specific legal questions. Advise on model licensing and open-weight model terms, customer data use, and IP rights in inputs and outputs.
  • Partner with Security. Support incident response, breach notification analysis, vulnerability disclosure, and customer trust materials, including SOC 2 and ISO 27001.
  • Track the regulatory landscape. Follow developments in AI, privacy, and cloud regulation, including the EU AI Act and U.S. federal and state law. Turn them into practical guidance and input for the product roadmap.
  • Advise on export controls and trade compliance for AI compute and cloud services.
  • Help teams answer routine questions themselves through training, playbooks, and templates.
  • Manage outside counsel on specialized matters.

What You’ll Bring:
  • 4–6 years of legal experience at a top law firm, in-house, or both, with substantial exposure to product counseling, privacy, cybersecurity, or technology transactions
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure or platform services (IaaS/PaaS), such as cloud service agreements, SLAs, or shared responsibility models (strongly preferred)
  • A track record advising on AI/ML products, models, or data, including AI governance, model and data licensing, acceptable use, or AI regulatory compliance such as the EU AI Act
  • Working knowledge of global privacy laws and emerging AI regulatory frameworks
  • Familiarity with established product legal practices (product review, privacy programs, AI governance, customer trust commitments) and an interest in adapting them for a high-growth company
  • A builder’s mindset: you’re energized by creating processes, templates, and programs from scratch, with guidance from senior counsel
  • Ownership and initiative: you handle day-to-day product questions on your own and know when to escalate
  • A growth orientation: you seek out feedback and learn quickly
  • Pragmatic, commercially minded judgment: you know when “good enough” is the right answer, and you help teams find a path to yes
  • Real curiosity about how AI and infrastructure technology works, and a willingness to dig into the technical details
  • Clear, plain-language communication about legal risk, and the ability to earn the trust of stakeholders
  • Composure in a fast-moving environment with limited direction and imperfect information, while balancing competing priorities and multiple time-sensitive matters
  • Experience at an established cloud, infrastructure, semiconductor, or AI company (preferred); startup or high-growth experience is a plus
  • A JD or equivalent law degree from an accredited institution, plus active bar admission in good standing or other authorization to practice law

Why Join Us:
  • Purposeful Hiring: You’re not here by accident, and neither is anyone else. Every teammate is handpicked with intention because who we build with matters.
  • Builders Wanted: You’re not just riding the rocket ship, you’re building it. Your work directly shapes the trajectory of our company.
  • Mission-Driven Work: We’re here to make a real impact. Our mission fuels everything we do.
  • Tackling Hard Problems: If easy isn’t your thing, you’re in the right place. We solve some of the most complex and exciting challenges in our space.
  • Excellence Is The Standard: High performance isn’t just encouraged, it’s the baseline. And it’s contagious.

Compensation
Groq is committed to providing competitive compensation through our Total Cash philosophy, which incorporates potential bonus value directly into base pay. The total cash salary range for this position, which is inclusive of the potential bonus value, is $186,600–$252,400, with individual placement determined by your geographic location, experience, skills, and alignment with internal compensation standards. This range is specific to candidates located in the United States. Compensation for international candidates will vary based on local market dynamics. Beyond cash compensation, Groq also offers a Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Program and a robust suite of employee benefits.

About your environment

Cancer Council Victoria: Technology x Impact

Since our establishment in 1936, Cancer Council Victoria has developed an international reputation for our innovative work in cancer research, prevention and support. As an independent, not-for-profit organisation, we play a leading role in reducing the impact of all cancers on all people.

The Corporate Services Division incorporates governance, finance, legal, risk, information technology, property and logistics. The focus of the Division is to ensure Cancer Council's Corporate Services operate to the highest standards of efficiency and effectiveness to ensure compliance and support the organisation to deliver on its Strategic Priorities. The Division also works to ensure the protection and optimisation of the Council's financial and business assets, and reputation.

Part of Corporate Services Division, the IT team includes Digital Team, Operations Team and the AI Program Team.

At Cancer Council Victoria we believe in impactful technology

Our digital vision is to prevent cancer, empower patients and save lives through connection, collaboration and innovation. The Information Technology (IT) team champions this vision and supports the rest of the organisation in its realisation. We deliver the software platforms, infrastructure, support, security and services that enable CCV as a digital-first organisation.

We are not just technologists who craft top-end solutions, our team creates a direct impact for all Victorians and Australians who are affected by cancer. So, if you're someone who is seeking a meaningful technology career, you will fit right in with us.

We are building a high-performing technology team geared for collaborative and agile ways-of-working.

Are you looking to develop your skills, try new things and make a meaningful impact? If so, this is the place for you. At Cancer Council Victoria, you will have the opportunity to hone your craft using the latest technologies and extend your skills across adjacent technology domains.

About your opportunity

This role is perfect for those who are looking for growth in their data career while also making a real difference for those affected by cancer.

Being a part of the centralised Digital Team, your role will:

  • Design, build and maintain enterprise Power BI dashboards and reports to visualise data sets.
  • Explore data sets to identify trends, patterns, and anomalies including data model optimisation in SNOWFLAKE.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of statistical models and algorithms.
  • Assist in building and maintaining data pipelines for efficient FABRIC ELT/ETL utilising SNOWFLAKE cloud data warehouse platform.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders and teams to improve data quality assurance efforts to ensure accuracy and reliability of data.
  • Help identify opportunities for process improvement and data-driven decision-making.

All about you

  • Relevant tertiary degree in Data Engineering or related field and/or experience in Data and Analytics role
  • Strong understanding of data manipulation, data structures, and algorithms.
  • Proficiency in modern cloud data platform such as SNOWFLAKE.
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, or SQL.
  • Proficiency with data visualisation tools such as Power BI and DAX.
  • Basic knowledge of statistical concepts and techniques.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong communication skills to convey complex findings to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Eagerness to learn and adapt to new technologies and methodologies.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

What we can offer you

  • Work for purpose: Contribute to our powerful mission to reduce the impact of cancer through prevention, support, and research.
  • Salary: $89,299 to $98,632 base salary per annum (pro rata for part-time), commensurate with experience, plus 12% superannuation and 17.5% annual leave loading.
  • Not-for-profit salary packaging benefits: Increase your take-home pay by paying certain expenses using your pre-tax salary — up to $15,900 in living expenses plus $2,650 in meals and entertainment annually.
  • Generous leave: Study leave, cultural and ceremonial leave, blood donation leave, gender affirmation leave, paid parental leave, and up to 3 days of leave between Christmas Day and New Year's Day. Refer to our Enterprise Agreement for more information.
  • Flexible and hybrid work: A range of options to support work-life balance, including a mix of working from home and our modern office at 200 Victoria Parade, East Melbourne.
  • Health and wellbeing support: Comprehensive employee assistance program, flu vaccinations, and discounted health insurance.
  • Growth and development opportunities: Study support, plus in-house, external, and online learning programs.
  • Workplace culture: A collaborative, inclusive and purpose-driven workplace - recognised with the Best Workplace Award.

To apply and for more info

Cancer Council will only contact applicants that are shortlisted for interview. We are also unable to respond to recruitment agency enquiries.

All offers of employment will be made subject to satisfactory completion of employment checks including evidence of right to work in Australia, a National Police Check and a Working with Children Check (as required).

Applications close 18 November 2026 at 11:59pm.

Cancer Council Victoria aspires to have a workforce that reflects the diverse community we serve. We're proud to foster a culture of belonging where our people can thrive.

We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally and linguistically diverse communities, people living with disability, neurodivergent people, LGBTIQA+ people, people of all ages, and parents and carers. If you need any adjustments to the recruitment process at any stage, please let us know. We'll work with you to make it accessible.
