title: Financial Aid Director
description:
About the Role

The Financial Aid Director provides strategic and operational leadership for the University's financial aid programs and services. The role is responsible for ensuring compliance with all federal, state, and institutional regulations governing student financial assistance while supporting student access, retention, and success.

Reporting to the Vice President of Student Affairs, the Financial Aid Director oversees the administration of financial aid programs, student loan processing, satisfactory academic progress monitoring, Title IV compliance, financial aid counseling, reporting, audits, and departmental operations. The position serves as the University's primary subject matter expert on financial aid regulations and works collaboratively with Enrollment, Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, Finance, and other institutional stakeholders to support the student experience.

The Financial Aid Director supervises Financial Aid staff and ensures that the University's financial aid practices promote regulatory compliance, operational excellence, student service, and institutional effectiveness.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Higher Education Administration, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Student Affairs, or a related field.
  • Five years of progressively responsible experience in financial aid administration within a higher education environment.
  • Demonstrated experience administering Title IV financial aid programs, regulations, compliance requirements, and reporting obligations.
  • Experience interpreting and applying federal and state financial aid regulations.
  • Experience with student information systems, financial aid management systems, and related technology platforms.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise, train, and develop staff.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Higher Education Administration, Business Administration, Student Affairs, Finance, or a related field.
  • Seven or more years of financial aid administration experience.
  • Previous experience leading a financial aid office or department.
  • Experience serving as a School Certifying Official (SCO).
  • Experience with financial aid audits, program reviews, accreditation activities, and federal reporting.
  • Experience developing policies, procedures, and operational controls.
  • Knowledge of enrollment management and student retention strategies.
  • Experience with federal audits, program reviews, FISAP preparation, and campus-based aid administration.
  • Experience presenting financial aid information to students, families, faculty, staff, and external audiences.

Key Responsibilities

FINANCIAL AID ADMINISTRATION & COMPLIANCE

  • Direct and oversee the administration of all federal, state, institutional, and external financial aid programs.
  • Ensure institutional compliance with all applicable financial aid regulations, policies, and reporting requirements.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain financial aid policies, procedures, and internal controls.
  • Monitor financial aid packaging and awarding processes to ensure consistency, compliance, and accuracy.
  • Oversee administration of Veterans Affairs (VA) educational benefits programs.
  • Ensure timely certification of student enrollments and reporting of enrollment changes through applicable VA systems.
  • Maintain compliance with VA regulations, audits, reporting requirements, and institutional approvals.
  • Serve as the University's School Certifying Official (SCO) or supervise SCO activities.
  • Oversee Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) processes and compliance.
  • Oversee Return of Title IV Funds (R2T4) calculations and related regulatory requirements.
  • Administer student loan processes and ensure accurate reporting to federal agencies and related systems.
  • Maintain regulatory readiness for audits, program reviews, and accreditation activities.

FINANCIAL OPERATIONS & REPORTING

  • Oversee reconciliation processes for all financial aid funds and programs.
  • Collaborate with Finance, Student Accounts, HR, and other departments to ensure accurate and timely financial aid transactions.
  • Prepare and submit required federal, state, institutional, and external reports, including FISAP and other compliance-related filings.
  • Maintain accurate records, documentation, and audit trails for all financial aid activities.
  • Monitor fund utilization and ensure compliance with allocation and expenditure requirements.
  • Assist with departmental budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning activities.

STUDENT SERVICE & COUNSELING

  • Provide leadership for student-centered financial aid services.
  • Counsel students and families regarding financial aid eligibility, financing options, satisfactory academic progress requirements, and related concerns.
  • Oversee professional judgment, special circumstances, and appeals processes.
  • Communicate financial aid policies and procedures clearly and effectively to students and families.
  • Ensure timely and accurate responses to financial aid inquiries.

FEDERAL WORK STUDY AND CAMPUS-BASED PROGRAM MANAGEMENT

  • Administer and oversee Federal Work Study and Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant programs.
  • Develop annual awarding methodologies and monitor expenditures to ensure compliance with federal allocation requirements.
  • Coordinate payroll reconciliation and federal reporting for campus-based aid programs.

APPEALS & SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES ADMINISTRATION

  • Establish and oversee financial aid appeals processes and committees.
  • Review and administer appeals related to SAP, special circumstances, dependency overrides, and other allowable adjustments.
  • Review and determine eligibility for dependency overrides, special circumstances appeals, unusual circumstances reviews, and satisfactory academic progress appeals.
  • Chair or oversee financial aid appeals committees and related review processes.
  • Ensure appeals are processed consistently and in compliance with applicable regulations.
  • Communicate appeal outcomes and available options to students.

LEADERSHIP & STAFF DEVELOPMENT

  • Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and performance management for Financial Aid staff.
  • Establish departmental goals, priorities, and service standards.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and exceptional service.
  • Conduct regular staff meetings and professional development activities.
  • Participate in hiring, onboarding, training, and evaluation of department personnel.

OUTREACH, COMMUNICATION & INSTITUTIONAL COLLABORATION

  • Develop and deliver financial aid presentations, workshops, and educational programs.
  • Support enrollment, recruitment, and retention initiatives through financial aid outreach efforts.
  • Maintain and update financial aid publications, forms, website content, and student communications.
  • Collaborate with Enrollment Management, Academic Affairs, Student Affairs, Finance, Admissions, Marketing, and other departments to enhance student success.
  • Serve as a resource to faculty and staff regarding financial aid policies and processes.

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

  • Maintain current knowledge of federal and state financial aid regulations and industry best practices.
  • Participate in professional associations, conferences, training programs, and continuing education activities.
  • Monitor emerging trends and regulatory developments impacting higher education financial aid administration.
  • Monitor and report on budget variances, providing recommendations for corrective action.
  • Ensure effective utilization of resources across all departments under their supervision.

Skills Requirements

  • Comprehensive knowledge of federal and state financial aid regulations, Title IV programs, and compliance requirements.
  • Expertise in financial aid administration, including awarding, packaging, verification, satisfactory academic progress (SAP), and Return of Title IV Funds (R2T4) processes.
  • Knowledge of Veterans Affairs educational benefits programs and reporting requirements.
  • Knowledge of FISAP preparation, reconciliation, and campus-based aid administration.
  • Experience with NSLDS, COD, EdConnect, FAFSA processing, and financial aid management systems.
  • Strong leadership, staff supervision, coaching, and team development skills.
  • Ability to interpret and apply complex regulations, policies, and procedures while ensuring institutional compliance.
  • Proficiency in financial reporting, reconciliation, audits, and data analysis.
  • Experience with student information systems, financial aid management systems, and related technology platforms.
  • Strong strategic planning, operational management, and process improvement capabilities.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving, decision-making, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to build collaborative relationships across departments and effectively support institutional goals.
  • Strong commitment to student service, confidentiality, professionalism, and continuous improvement.

title: Dining Services Director
description:
Pay Range: $60,000-$65,000

The Dining Services Director leads the execution of the signature dining services program at the community. He or she provides friendly, responsive service to create an exceptional dining experience for all of our residents. Each Dining Services Director’s primary objective is to exhibit the core values of Commonwealth Senior Living and provide a memorable dining experience for the residents.

Full-time associates are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, which may include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability options
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan
  • Paid time off
  • Employee assistance program
  • Additional voluntary benefits

Qualifications

• Certification in the Food Handlers Course or equivalent

• Previous management experience in the food service industry.

• Ability to read and write English.

• Willingness and ability to learn new tasks

• Must be available to work varied shifts and weekends.

• Ability to lift heavy objects; stand and walk short distances throughout the day. Ability to tolerate heat from the kitchen.

• Must be free of communicable diseases.

Areas of Primary Responsibility

• Prepare and serve nutritious meals to our residents in a safe sanitary manner in accordance with Public Health Regulations, and in compliance with Sanitation Code.

• Prepare food for regular and therapeutic diets according to the planned menu and written doctors’ orders.

• Ensure that the proper quantity of food is prepared and in accordance with established time schedules.

• Prepare food for special events as instructed by the Executive Director.

• Maintain costs within budgeted parameters.

• Use proper technique to taste prepared food to ensure quality taste and palatability prior to service.

• Maintain the proper temperature of food during preparation and service. Record temperatures of food according to established policy.

• Report all hazardous and malfunctioning equipment to the Executive Director.

• Make recommendations to the Director of Dining Services regarding improvements in recipes, menus, productions and service of food, equipment, etc. to enhance the quality of the food service.

• Attend and participate in workshops, seminars and in-services, to keep abreast of current changes in the health care field, as well as maintain a professional status.

• Skilled in the selection of personnel and management of staff to meet the needs of the department and entire community.

• Assist in scheduling department working hours, personnel, work assignments, etc. to maintain quality resident care.

• Routinely inspect the dietary area and practices for compliance with current applicable regulations and as requested by the Director.

• Develop and utilize comprehensive inventory control procedures.

• Purchase food, supplies, and equipment, as required to meet the needs of the department.

• Ensure that a stock of staple/non-staple food, supplies, equipment, etc., is maintained at adequate levels at all times to perform departmental functions.

• Ensure that there is always a 72-hour emergency food and drinking water supply per regulations.

• Maintain confidentiality of all pertinent resident care information to ensure resident rights are protected.

• Supervise and manage schedules and tasks of all dining department associates.

• Other duties as assigned.

Culture Ambassador

• Models the core values of the company:

  • We Care About People
  • We Do the Right Thing
  • We are Passionate, Have Fun, and Celebrate Success
  • We Speak Up! It’s Our Responsibility
  • We Take Ownership and Add Value
  • We are Respectful

• Ensures all personnel exemplify the core values of the company at all times.

• Create and drive the sales culture.

title: Startup Coordinator
description:
Job Summary:

Step into a role where your expertise directly shapes the success of a cutting‑edge facility. Start-up Coordinators are the dynamic presence on the front-line which oversees multi-disciplinary efforts associated with facility expansion and start up. From coordination efforts associated with design and construction, to administrative efforts involving training material and procedure development, to complex integrated systems testing and system turnover for full operational readiness. Few positions are going to have the exposure to the full gamut of business practices such as engineering, construction, project controls, operations, quality, regulatory and many more. This is your opportunity to be a vital piece towards American Nuclear prominence.

What You Will Do:

In this role, you will coordinate different processes for different systems in different facilities all simultaneously. Cascades require numerous support systems and facilities to allow for successful production, all of these processes require rigorous testing, trained and qualified operators, and detailed procedures. Start-up Coordinators coordinate end‑to‑end start‑up scope from CFC through installation, testing, turnover and closeout, partnering with the Engineering Modification Managers, Operations Interface Managers, and other system stakeholders while reporting to the Start-up Manager. To facilitate these objectives, Coordinators will be directly performing:

  • Leadership efforts in ensuring successful integrated systems testing and acceptance of cascades and balance-of-plant systems.
  • Administrative efforts in standing up the critical documents tracker for procedures, training modules, qualification cards, drill guides, drawings, and parts lists.
  • Coordination efforts through the use of trackers, status dashboards, and readiness reviews.
  • Problem identification and resolution through the use of business practices and software to ensure issues are forecasted, identified and driven to resolution.

Success in this position will largely be determined by:

  • Proactive communication and coordination regarding statuses and practices associated with system start-up,
  • On-time completion of integrated systems testing and turnover milestones,
  • Accurate and timely documentation,
  • Effective issue forecasting and resolution.

We’d Love to Hear from People With:

  • 3+ years of industrial, chemical, nuclear plant operations, maintenance, engineering, support experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience in similar rigorous industry or military job family
  • 2+ years of coordination, supervisory, or management experience
  • High-level Microsoft Office proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word, and Microsoft Visio
  • Ability to obtain (or already possess) a “Q” clearance

A Successful Candidate Brings:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or the physical sciences, Business Management, or equivalent technical/military experience
  • 5+ years of industrial, chemical, nuclear plant operations, maintenance, engineering, support experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience in a similar rigorous industry or military job family
  • 5+ years of management or supervisory experience, preferably within Operations, Maintenance, or Engineering
  • Currently possesses a Q or L clearance.

Pay:

Estimated Starting Base Salary Range: $92,915 - $154,858. This position is bonus eligible. Centrus considers several factors when extending job offers, including but not limited to candidates’ key skills, relevant work experience, and education/training/certifications. While the posted range reflects the anticipated hiring range for this position, compensation above the range may be considered for candidates with exceptional qualifications and directly relevant experience.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

This position will require a pre­-employment background check and a pre-employment drug test.

Centrus Energy and all subsidiaries shall abide by the applicable legal requirements. We prohibit discrimination against qualified individuals based on their status as protected veterans or individuals with disabilities and prohibit discrimination against all individuals based on their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or national origin.

This position requires the successful candidate to obtain and maintain a Q security clearance. Candidates for positions requiring a security clearance are required to be tested for the absence of any illegal drug as defined in 10 CFR 707.4 prior to an offer of employment being made. In addition, once employed, employees will become part of a random drug testing program and may also be tested in the event of any incident causing injury or causing damage to property, or if it is determined that there is a reasonable suspicion the employee is under the influence of drugs or alcohol. This position will require preemployment background check on the part of the Company and in order to receive a Q security clearance, a background investigation by the Federal government. Subsequent Federal government reinvestigations may be required.

Centrus Energy Corp. is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Airport Control Shift Lead
description:
The Airport Control Shift Lead leads and coordinates Heathrow’s Airport Control operations in APOC, ensuring all day response to a wide range of incidents and enquiries across the airport. They are subject matter experts in SOPs, guiding the team during incidents, maintaining standards, and overseeing complex or high-impact situations while liaising with key stakeholders. They also manage team performance, act as a key escalation point, and serve as a link between operational teams and senior airport leadership.

Shift Pattern: 12 hour shifts, both early and late - 4 on 4 off pattern. Please note this role requires CTC clearance which requires UK residency for the past 3 years.

  • Lead and coordinate day-to-day Airport Control operations, acting as the primary link with AOM, ACM/ACOM, and wider stakeholders, while maintaining situational awareness during incidents.
  • Line manage and support the team (OLCs/OCs), overseeing wellbeing, performance, training, and ensuring adequate shift coverage and effective time management.
  • Oversee incident management, ensuring SOPs are followed, accurate records are logged, and appropriate responses/resources are deployed for alarms, emergencies, and enquiries.
  • Monitor systems, faults, and incident trackers (e.g. DORIS), ensuring timely resolution, escalation of critical issues, and operational readiness at all times.
  • Act as the key escalation point and liaison during incidents, coordinating communication between operational teams, senior management, and external partners.
  • Drive operational excellence through continuous improvement, consistent standards, stakeholder service, and effective handovers, briefings, and team coordination.

  • Ability to remain calm and perform effectively under pressure in a complex, fast-paced environment.

  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing demands effectively.

  • Effective communication and influencing skills across all levels, including internal teams, external partners and control authorities.

  • Ability to demonstrate sound judgement and decision-making when handling sensitive incidents or challenging situations.

  • Handles confidential and sensitive information with discretion, professionalism and integrity.

  • Able to build strong working relationships, challenge constructively where appropriate, and ensure compliance with established procedures and standards.

Ideally:

  • Experience in Airport Operations, ideally with at least 12 months in a multi-stakeholder operational environment.
  • Familiarity with Heathrow’s terminal and airfield geography.
  • Ability to identify and implement operational improvements and new ways of working.

title: Benefit Programs Specialist II
description:
Title Description- Benefit Programs Specialist II represents the full-performance level in the Benefit Programs Specialist occupational group. Employees’ responsibilities are related to the determination and re-determination of eligibility of individuals and families for financial assistance, food stamps, medical assistance, and for other social services’ benefit programs. The work is performed within established policies, procedures and guidelines, but certain aspects of eligibility determination require independent judgment, especially as related to evaluation of social factors influencing eligibility. Employees seek supervisory help for difficult or unusual situations only. The Benefit Programs Specialist II is distinguished from the Benefit Programs Specialist III by the latter’s performing advanced technical work requiring depth and breadth of knowledge to understand, analyze and act on complex cases. Also, the Benefit Programs Specialist III serves as a technical resource for others regarding social services’ eligibility programs.

General Work Tasks (Illustrative Only) –
  • Interviews persons for assistance, obtains necessary information, and re-determines their continuing eligibility;
  • Explains benefit programs and determines reasons and need for assistance;
  • Processes applications for financial assistance and diversion; determines eligibility for assistance and benefit levels using automated systems and manual methods;
  • Interprets policies and procedures applicable to the various programs;
  • Monitors cases for changes in recipient circumstances, and implements changes to appropriately reflect benefit level within guidelines;
  • Evaluates employability status of clients and explores potential sources of income; explains client responsibilities, rights and program availability;
  • Refers clients to service worker as the result of overall assessment of situation; prepares reports and maintains client records;
  • Identifies possible fraud and makes appropriate referrals; evaluates consistency and completeness of data secured, and where indicated substantiates its accuracy;
  • Explains programs and rights/responsibilities of applicants and recipients;
  • Explores other possible sources of income;
  • Computes assistance plans;
  • Determines the amount of allowances for special circumstance items such as household equipment;
  • Identifies clearly discernible social problems and makes referrals to Social Workers;
  • Provides applicants or recipients with information about other agencies where they may go for services as needed.
  • Explains a variety of programs under the social services umbrella such as employment services, child support services and child care services.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Knowledge- Working knowledge of: practices of public service organizations; economic and basic human behavior; financial assistance programs sufficient to determine/re-determine eligibility for benefits; eligibility requirements for social service assistance as outlined by State, Local and Federal guidelines, regulations and policies; mathematics to calculate percentages, formulas and averages to solve mathematical problems; and interviewing techniques such as data collection and investigation.

Skills- Skill in operating a personal computer and the associated office and agency software.

Abilities- Demonstrated ability to: communicate effectively both orally and in writing with broad spectrum of individuals to include, but not limited to, customers, employers, courts, and medical professionals in person and on the phone; interview, gather information, re-evaluate each client’s situation, and make referrals; determine a client’s ownership share in situations; make mathematical computations; analyze information and determine from a variety of sources missing information and gaps; apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written or oral form; use various types of automated technology to establish and maintain case records, access data such as estates, retirement accounts, and real estate, reports, and manipulate data; maintain professional ethics related to confidentiality; exercise sound judgment, discretion, tact and resourcefulness in solving problems and drawing logical conclusions; and establish and maintain effective working relationships with applicants and recipients, other public and private agencies, associates, and the public in a positive and tactful manner under sometimes stressful situations.

Education and Experience- Same as required in Benefit Program Specialist I with experience in benefit programs, use of computer software and hardware, and completion of required Benefit Programs training OR any equivalent combination of training and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities.
